articles.title: ALIoTh: Orchestrating Multi-Agent LLMs for Autonomous IoT Penetration Testing
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.25809v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Penetration testing in Internet of Things (IoT) environments, especially those composed of various different devices, e.g., smart plugs, smart cameras, and smart doors, presents great challenges across the phases of information gathering, attack surface enumeration, privilege escalation, and lateral movement. This paper introduces ALIoTh, a multi-agent, workflow-driven penetration testing framework that integrates Large Language Models agents within a Self-Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Self-RAG) architecture to autonomously identify and exploit vulnerabilities in IoT and Industrial-IoT (IIoT) environments. By leveraging state-of-the-art language models and orchestrating specialized agents via the LangGraph framework, ALIoTh dynamically plans and executes a full-spectrum offensive pipeline. This includes network, devices, and service enumeration, vulnerability assessment, payload generation, reverse shell deployment, and privilege escalation on each device. The Self-RAG mechanism equips expert agents with contextual access to IoT security knowledge, e.g., related documentation, tool manuals, and known attack techniques, enhancing their reasoning capabilities in scenarios involving multiple device exploitation and group policy manipulation.

articles.summary_ja: スマートプラグやスマートカメラ等の多様なIoT/IIoT環境における侵入テストの自動化を目的とした研究論文である。LangGraphフレームワークとSelf-RAGアーキテクチャを活用し、専門エージェントを連携させてネットワーク・機器・サービスの列挙から脆弱性評価、ペイロード生成、特権昇格までを自律実行するALIoThを提案した。ドキュメントやツールマニュアルを参照することで、複数機器の侵害シナリオにおいて推論能力を向上させている。

articles.title: Hardening JavaScript Programs against LLM-Based Vulnerability Detection
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.25718v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: JavaScript programs are often distributed as source code, so attackers can analyze them for vulnerabilities. LLM-based vulnerability detection agents now make this analysis much easier. To mitigate this emerging threat, we present AntiAgent, a defense that lets developers harden their programs against such detection agents. AntiAgent transforms a program before release to impede an agent's analysis. To find effective transformations, AntiAgent evolves a corpus of programs with known vulnerabilities and traces how a detection agent analyzes each evolved version. It keeps the versions on which the agent misses or misreports the vulnerability and extracts their transformations into reusable rules. To protect a new program, AntiAgent carefully divides the task between an LLM and the rules, so that the transformations adapt to the program while preserving its semantics.
  We evaluate AntiAgent on real-world JavaScript applications against four detection agents, including Claude Code and Codex. AntiAgent reduces the number of vulnerabilities that each agent detects by 52.0-60.7%, outperforming the conventional obfuscator JS-Obfuscator and the LLM-based transformation method FPA on every agent. The transformed programs pass all project tests, indicating that AntiAgent preserves the original program semantics. The transformation rules also remain effective on vulnerability types absent from the corpus and on programs written in another language like Python.
articles.title_ja: LLMベースの脆弱性検出に対するJavaScriptプログラムの堅牢化手法「AntiAgent」

articles.title: SCARVA: Interpretable Agentic Reasoning in Software Supply-Chain Analysis
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.26131v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Complex applications may inherit security vulnerabilities from their dependencies, though a vulnerable dependency does not necessarily endanger the application. Existing tools flag dependencies associated with public vulnerabilities, and more advanced ones analyze the call graph to assess whether the vulnerable code is reachable. However, these approaches are limited to specific programming languages and ecosystems. LLM agents are promising candidates for this task, yet they hallucinate, take shortcuts, and reward hack. As these behaviors are opaque, the agents' conclusions may not be trusted.
  We present SCARVA a framework designed to produce interpretable reports. SCARVA combines advanced agent reasoning with an evidence-collection methodology that assesses the agent's analysis and improves its trustworthiness. Specifically, the ANALYST performs a software security assessment while SCARVA records every tool call, file access, and web request. Then, one or more independent JUDGE agents inspect the ANALYST's result and produce an evidence-backed report. We evaluate SCARVA on 54 manually curated cases, balanced across exploitable, non-exploitable, and vulnerability-free projects, using both open-weight and frontier models. The best ANALYST model, Qwen 3.8, reaches 82% balanced accuracy and surpasses the evaluated proprietary models. Human annotation validates the JUDGE findings: Claude Opus 5.5 performs best, agreeing with annotators in 94% of claim checks. Finally, we discuss the most common failure modes of agents on supply-chain vulnerability assessment.
articles.title_ja: SCARVA：ソフトウェアサプライチェーン分析における説明可能なエージェント推論
articles.summary_ja: 依存パッケージの脆弱性到達可能性評価において、LLMエージェントのハルシネーションや不透明性を解決するフレームワークSCARVAの論文である。セキュリティ評価を実施するANALYSTエージェントの全ツール呼出し・ファイルアクセス・Web要求を記録し、独立したJUDGEエージェントが監査して証拠付きレポートを作成する。キュレーションされた54件の検証において、ANALYST（Qwen 3.8）は82%の均衡精度を達成し、JUDGE（Claude Opus 5.5）は人手アノテーションと94%の一致を示した。
articles.insight: SCA（ソフトウェアサプライチェーン解析）における到達可能性判断にエージェントを活用する際、監査可能な証拠記録と独立した検証（JUDGE）機構を設けるアプローチは、誤検知低減と説明責任の確保に極めて有効である。AIエージェントのセキュリティ監査実務において、ツール呼び出しログに基づく監査追跡の標準化が求められる。

articles.title: Behavioral Containment: Source-to-Binary Function Matching for 1-Day Vulnerability Detection
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.25394v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vulnerabilities in reused open-source code often propagate into deployed binaries. Detecting them requires source-to-binary function matching, which locates the affected source function in a binary. Applying prior binary-to-binary approaches to this task would require compiling the source code with the same build configuration as the target binary, which is usually unavailable. Decompiling the binary does not make prior source-to-source approaches work either, because decompiled code differs substantially from the original source code.
  We observe that compilation transforms the code of a function but largely preserves its behavior. A binary function that implements a source function therefore contains its behavior, a property we call behavioral containment. Building on this, we present SBIND, which decompiles the binary and checks behavioral containment instead of comparing code. SBIND represents each function by behavioral paths, sequences of normalized operations from its entry to its exits, and aligns source paths with binary paths in order. To detect 1-day vulnerabilities, SBIND compares the binary with the vulnerable and the patched source only on the paths through the changed lines. On stripped binaries built with two compilers, two optimization levels, and four architectures, SBIND ranks the correct function first in 77.87% of 32,008 searches, against 45.69% for the state-of-the-art approach SBridge. On 26 1-day CVEs, SBIND reaches an F1 score of 0.70 on stripped binaries, against 0.51 for SBridge. Our replication of SBridge also revealed several issues in its implementation and evaluation, and its authors have acknowledged them.
articles.title_ja: バイナリとソースコードの比較による1-day脆弱性検知手法「SBIND」
articles.summary_ja: オープンソースコードの脆弱性がバイナリに混入する問題に対処するため、研究者らは「SBIND」と呼ばれる新しいソース・バイナリ間関数マッチング手法を提案した。コンパイル後もコードの動作が保持される「行動的包含（behavioral containment）」の性質に着目し、コードではなくパスの正規化された操作で比較を行う。32,008件の検索において、SBINDは正解関数を77.87%の確率で最上位にランクインさせ、既存手法を上回る性能を示した。26件の1-day CVEに対しても、F1スコア0.70を達成している。
articles.insight: ソースコードの脆弱性がビルド環境の違いや難読化を経たバイナリでどのように継承・検出されるかを評価する上で重要な研究である。SCAやバイナリ解析ツールにおいて、コードの構文一致ではなく動作ベースのマッチングを取り入れることで、誤検知を減らせる可能性がある。実務では、社内製バイナリやサードパーティ製コンポーネントの脆弱性追跡にどのように適用できるか検証が求められる。
articles.importance_reason: 既存のバイナリマッチング手法の限界を克服し、1-day脆弱性検知の精度を大きく向上させる新しいアプローチを提示しているため。

articles.title: Static Analysis Guidance for Secure LLM Code Generation
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.26312v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Static analyzers are cheap and widely deployed, which makes their reports a candidate feedback signal for secure LLM code generation. Existing approaches place the analyzer inside an iterative repair loop with intermediate steps, which is costly and makes it hard to isolate the report's effect on the model. We introduce two strategies that give the finding to the model during generation. When the analyzer raises an alert, generation is rolled back, and the finding is inserted either as a code comment (Comment) or in the user message (Steering). We compare them with two iterative approaches and a control without the analyzer, across three models and three Python benchmarks, and we measure security using each benchmark's oracle. Guidance during generation is cheap and can be effective, at 0.9 to 1.9 times the baseline's output tokens against up to 24.1 times for iterative approaches. With DeepSeek-V4.1-flash on RiskyPy, Steering raises the share of functional and secure programs from 52.5% to 64.4%, close to the best iterative approach (66.2%) while using less than a fifth of the tokens. A per-rule analysis shows that rules with a local fix benefit most, and replacing the XML parser is net-positive on two of the three models. The study also identifies when guidance should not be applied. Analyzers flag at most 5.6% of the functional but insecure programs on SecEvalPlus, leaving little guidance to act on. When a static analysis alert (warning or error) contradicts the task, models tend to follow the analyzer and break the program. The two Qwen2.5 models often fail when the fix requires restructuring the code. These results indicate that static-analysis guidance is worth applying with a capable model, on rules with a local fix, and after filtering alerts that conflict with the task specification.

articles.title: SkillBridge: Cost-Aware Diagnosis and Repair of Cross-OS Compatibility Defects in Agent Skills
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.26256v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents increasingly reuse executable capabilities through skills, but a skill that works on one OS may fail on another because OS assumptions are spread across guide text, scripts, metadata, install contracts, and local entrypoints. Diagnosing such failures by running every skill on every OS is expensive: many executions spend model tokens, runner time, and review effort before revealing whether the failure is truly OS-related. We present SkillBridge, a contract-based workflow with three stages: static analysis, dynamic validation, and repair. SkillBridge first screens 3,270 skill-target-OS cases, covering 1,090 skills across Linux, macOS, and Windows, to find OS-sensitive contract evidence. It then runs dynamic tasks and root-cause review on selected cases to confirm whether a failure is caused by an OS assumption, and repairs the contract field that caused the failure, such as guide text, package scripts, dependencies, or platform declarations. Repair raises the reviewer-judged target-task pass rate from 30.6% to 38.4%, a gain of 7.8 percentage points. A retrospective Linux/macOS budget analysis further shows the efficiency effect: SkillBridge reaches 38 confirmed OS issues with 185 dynamic validations, where uniform random selection would require about 865 validations in expectation.
articles.title_ja: SkillBridge: エージェントスキルにおけるクロスOS互換性不具合のコスト考慮型診断と修復
articles.summary_ja: LLMエージェントが再利用する実行可能スキルにおいて、OS依存の差異による不具合を効率的に診断・修復するフレームワーク「SkillBridge」が提案された。静的解析、動的検証、修復の3段階のコントラクトベースのワークフローにより、OS依存の不具合を特定し修正する。Linux、macOS、Windowsをまたぐ1,090スキルを対象とした評価では、タスクのパス率が30.6%から38.4%へ向上し、動的検証の効率も大幅に改善されたことが示されている。
articles.insight: AIエージェントが利用するスキルやツール群におけるクロスプラットフォーム環境での動作検証において、静的解析を組み合わせたコスト効率の高い診断アプローチが有効であることを示している。エージェントセキュリティの実務においては、エージェントが呼び出す外部スキルやツール群の実行環境の差異や依存関係をどのように検証・管理するかという課題への示唆となる。
articles.importance_reason: AIエージェントのスキル実行における互換性診断と自動修復に関する具体的な研究成果であり、今後のエージェント運用コスト削減と安全性確保に寄与するため。

articles.title: Newly Patched VMware vCenter Flaw Exploited as Zero-Day by Chinese APT
articles.summary:
Google says a China-linked espionage group exploited a critical VMware vCenter authentication bypass before Broadcom released a patch.

The post Newly Patched VMware vCenter Flaw Exploited as Zero-Day by Chinese APT appeared first on SecurityWeek.

articles.summary_ja: Googleの調査によると、中国関連のスパイ組織がVMware vCenterにおける重大な認証バイパス脆弱性を、Broadcomが修正パッチを公開する前にゼロデイ攻撃として悪用していたことが明らかになりました。攻撃者は修正前の防御の隙を突いて組織へ侵入を試みていました。ベンダーによる修正パッチ提供と同時に、すでに攻撃事例が存在する前提での迅速な対応が求められます。

articles.title: ACaM: Automated Capability Modeling for Agentic AI Security
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.23507v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In agentic AI systems, an LLM invokes tools that hold standing access to credentials, private data, filesystems, and external services. Such agents are increasingly deployed without an answer to a basic question: what can an agent access, exfiltrate, and propagate, independent of what it is designed for or is observed to do? The question goes unanswered because existing approaches trust a tool's natural-language description as a proxy for its behavior. But nothing enforces that the description and its implementation agree. This gap is known as Description-Code Inconsistency (DCI). DCI enables a threat class called capability laundering, in which a tool's implementation contains dangerous behavior that its description omits. The behavior may come from incidental drift or a supply-chain compromise. It runs silently whenever an LLM invokes the tool for its stated, benign purpose. We present ACaM, a neurosymbolic approach to capability modeling that derives each tool's capabilities from its code, so a laundered capability cannot hide behind a benign description. In ACaM, static analysis grounds an LLM in code-derived facts, and no LLM output can override a fact that static analysis has established. The LLM supplies only the behavioral meaning that those facts cannot express. ACaM compiles agent source code into the Agent Capability Property Graph (ACPG) and uses it to reconstruct threat chains that span multiple tool calls. We evaluate ACaM on 43 real-world agents, including 9 multi-agent systems. On 24 manually annotated agents, it recovers capability properties with 98.3% macro-F1 and reconstructs injected threat chains with a score of 0.980, 8 points above the strongest baseline. Applied to all 43 unmodified agents, it discovers hundreds of structural vulnerabilities, ten of which we confirm with proof-of-concept exploits.
articles.title_ja: ACaM：エージェント型AIにおける機能ロンダリング検出に向けた自動化ケイパビリティモデリング
articles.summary_ja: LLMベースのエージェントシステムにおいて、ツールの自然言語による説明と実際のコード実装の乖離（DCI）により、危険な挙動が隠蔽される機能ロンダリングの脅威が存在する。本論文では、静的解析によってコードから抽出した事実をLLMにグラウンディングさせ、プロパティグラフ（ACPG）を構築して脅威チェーンを特定するACaMを提案している。43の実環境エージェントを用いた評価において、多数の構造的脆弱性を特定し、10件のPoC検証に成功している。
articles.insight: AIエージェントのツール呼び出しを安全に制御するには、ツールのプロンプト/説明文だけでなく実装コードの静的解析と権限検証を連携させることが不可欠である。診断実務においては、エージェントのツール実装に含まれる潜在的な権限濫用リスクを静的解析と動的チェーン追跡で検査するハーネスの導入が検討課題となる。SOCやエージェント設計者は、ツール実行時の権限境界やタスク連鎖の振る舞いをコードベースの事実に基づいて監視できているかを問う必要がある。
articles.importance_reason: AIエージェントのツール定義と実装乖離によるセキュリティ脅威を静的解析とLLMの統合で解決する手法を提示し、実PoC検証まで示しているため。

assessments: ペネトレーションテスト
business.evidence: Applied to all 43 unmodified agents, it discovers hundreds of structural vulnerabilities, ten of which we confirm with proof-of-concept exploits.

arXiv:2611.23947v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Network discovery, the identification of live hosts and their exposed services, is the first phase of every penetration test, and it is increasingly automated by harnesses driven by large language models (LLMs). To mitigate hallucinated or unsafe commands, recent work proposes inserting fast, non-generative decision models to validate actions prior to execution. This paper quantifies whether such validation improves discovery across three network scales (n = 10, 100, and 1,000) in a simulation calibrated on a 30-node containerized testbed. Our findings show that chunked batch dispatch recovers 92% to 100% of open ports in large-scale networks, whereas single-host dispatch collapses to under 6% due to context saturation and scan latency. Furthermore, at the measured proposal quality of the local model, decision gating increases its port recall from 75.5% to 89.0% on small networks and intercepts costly decoy tarpits, but it imposes additional latency on frontier models during early host discovery.

articles.title: LLMs for Software Vulnerability Prediction and Prioritization: A Review
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.23304v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Large language models have moved beyond vulnerability detection into prediction, assessment, exploitability estimation, risk assessment and prioritization, yet the evidence for this shift has not been synthesised separately from the detection literature. In this systematic literature review, we examine how LLMs are used across those five task classes, how well they perform against established baselines, and what prevents their operational adoption. Following a prespecified protocol, we identified 197 records, removed 53 duplicates, and excluded 103 records at title and abstract stage. We assessed 41 full texts and finally retained 23 primary studies published between 2024 and 2026 after a six-question quality assessment. The review contributes a five-class taxonomy ordered by decision outcome, a method taxonomy covering prompting, tuning and retrieval or agentic architectures, an evaluation-practice audit, a bounded performance synthesis, and a deployment-barrier analysis. The main findings are that (i) assessment is the largest class (9 of 23 studies), ahead of risk assessment and prioritization (7 each); (ii) reported accuracy is highest where the label space is tightest and is not stable across evaluation periods; (iii) explanation usability is an audited evidence gap rather than a demonstrated capability; and (iv) reproducibility is the weakest reported dimension. We conclude that present systems should support analyst judgement rather than replace it, and we specify three validation studies that would settle the open questions.
articles.title_ja: ソフトウェア脆弱性の予測・優先順位付けにおけるLLM活用動向の系統的レビュー
articles.summary_ja: 脆弱性の検知だけでなく、予測、評価、悪用可能性の推定、リスク評価、優先順位付けにおけるLLMの適用動向について、2024年から2026年までの主要研究23件を対象に系統的文献レビューを実施した。研究の多くは評価（Assessment）とリスク評価・優先順位付けに集中しており、ラベル空間が限定的な場合に高い精度を示す傾向が見られた。一方で、出力される説明の実用性や研究の再現性が実務導入における重大な課題であることが示されている。
articles.insight: LLMによる脆弱性管理の自動化は、単純な検出を超えてリスク評価や優先順位付けへの応用が進んでいるが、再現性の低さや説明性の不足が実運用の大きな障壁となっている。診断やExposure管理の実務においては、LLMをアナリストの代替とするのではなく、判断を支援する補助機能として設計することが現時点での現実的なアプローチである。CDC設計者は、LLMが出力したリスクスコアや優先度判断を人間のアナリストがどの基準で検証・承認するかという運用プロセスの確立を問う必要がある。

articles.title: Characterizing GitHub Security Actions Alerts For Web Application Tutorials
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.23967v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The high frequency of cybersecurity incidents involving web applications highlights the importance of secure software development practices. Static Application Security Testing (SAST) tools help identify potential vulnerabilities in source code without executing the code. Integrating SAST tools into GitHub Security Actions enables security alerts to be reported during development. However, the characteristics of these alerts can make them difficult for developers with limited security expertise to understand, prioritize, and address. Many tutorials for learning web application development also involve source code with security implications. We investigated the properties of SAST alerts relevant to this learning context. We analyzed 6,609 alerts from four default GitHub Security Actions configurations across 60 Django and Spring tutorial repositories. We evaluated the alerts along four dimensions: alert volume, alert relevance, conceptual breadth, and remediation usability. Of the 6,609 alerts, 3,750 (56.7\%) targeted tutorial-related files, while 2,859 (43.3\%) targeted other repository files. The configurations triggered between 34 and 646 distinct rules, and the five most frequently triggered rules accounted for 25.2\%--68.2\% of alerts, depending on the configuration. Across configurations, 0.4\%--32.1\% of alert messages named concrete framework or code constructs, and 0\%--8.1\% met our operational criteria for remediation specificity. Overall, default GitHub Security Actions report a diverse set of security alerts, but these alerts do not consistently focus on tutorial code or provide concrete guidance for addressing the reported issues.
articles.title_ja: WebチュートリアルにおけるGitHub Security Actionsアラートの特性分析
articles.summary_ja: Webアプリケーション開発のチュートリアルリポジトリを対象に、デフォルトのGitHub Security ActionsによるSASTアラートの特性を調査した研究。DjangoおよびSpringの60リポジトリから計6,609件のアラートを抽出し、量・関連性・概念的広がり・修正案の実用性の4軸で評価した。アラートの43.3%が教材外のファイルに起因し、修正指示の具体性を満たしたのは最大でも8.1%にとどまるなど、開発者の学習・修正支援における課題が示された。

articles.title: Mitigating fix reversal: Counterfactual constraints for function-level vulnerability detection
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.24489v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Function-level vulnerability detectors often exhibit fix reversal, assigning a higher vulnerability probability to a fixed version than to its vulnerable counterpart. Fixes usually lengthen functions, and larger length increases are associated with more severe reversal. Code-transformation experiments indicate that fix reversal mainly stems from a length shortcut: vulnerability probability increases with function length when content is fixed. We propose CFVul to address this problem. Sliding-window encoding covers complete functions, retaining fix information beyond the truncation boundary. During training, a content constraint encourages the vulnerable version to receive a higher vulnerability probability under a common length input. During inference, a length constraint averages vulnerability probabilities over fixed reference lengths, reducing the influence of actual length changes. On PrimeVul, CFVul achieves a fix-pair ranking metric, PairRank, of 59.4\%, exceeding the existing methods compared. For fixes that increase function length by more than 15\%, PairRank rises from CodeBERT's 25.8\% to 48.4\%. PairRank also improves in experiments with four additional models and three additional datasets. By weakening the length shortcut, CFVul reduces cases in which fixed versions receive higher vulnerability probabilities than vulnerable versions. It requires only existing fix pairs and applies to multiple pretrained code models, facilitating adoption in existing detectors.
engineering_topics: 評価基盤・データセット
articles.title_ja: 関数レベル脆弱性検出における修正逆転の緩和：反事実的制約CFVulの提案
articles.summary_ja: 関数レベルの機械学習ベース脆弱性検出器において、修正後コードのほうが脆弱と誤判定される「fix reversal」現象を調査した研究。この現象は修正に伴うコード長増加を脆弱性確率上昇と関連付ける「長さのショートカット」に起因すると特定された。提案手法CFVulはスライディングウィンドウと反事実的制約（訓練時の内容制約と推論時の長さ制約）を導入し、PrimeVulでのPairRankをCodeBERTの25.8%から48.4%へと向上させた。
articles.insight: AIを活用したコード診断モデルがコード行数の変化という表面的な特徴に過学習し、修正後コードをより危険と判断する実態が定量的かつ構造的に解明されている。AIによる脆弱性検出や修正提案ツールを実務に導入する際は、修正の有効性を再診断する段階で生じる誤検知・逆転現象を考慮したバリデーション機構が必要となる。AI診断の出力結果に対する検証パイプラインをどう構築すべきかが重要な論点となる。

articles.title: Beyond Stars: MTTX Brings Developer Responsiveness to Dependency Decisions, from Dashboard to IDE to GitHub Actions
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.23285v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern software reuses open-source packages as dependencies, and developers often choose among candidate packages with cheap signals, such as GitHub stars and download counts. However, such signals are easy to fake, so developers need signals that represent "observed behavior," such as how quickly the developers of a package respond to new dependency releases and to security fixes. Prior work computed these responsiveness metrics, MTTU (Mean Time To Update) dependencies and MTTR (Mean Time To Remediate) vulnerable dependencies, but only with a research prototype for a fixed set of packages. Therefore, developers cannot easily benefit from them or integrate them into their workflow. We present MTTX, an open-source tool that computes MTTU and MTTR with accurate historical dependency resolution for any package and given time window, and brings them into different phases of developer workflow. MTTX resolves each version constraint of npm, PyPI, and Cargo packages as of a past date, with data from the native registries or deps.dev and vulnerability data from OSV. We validated MTTX with 328 automated tests, and for 90 packages from prior work, we manually verified its dependency resolution at each historical release point and its MTTU and MTTR computation. Developers can use MTTX in an interactive web dashboard, an IDE extension, and a GitHub Action, which are all available from the project homepage at https://imranur-rahman.github.io/dependency-update-metrics/. We envision that package registries (e.g., npm) and metadata aggregators and intelligence platforms (e.g., deps.dev) will display these values on the package page, alongside download counts and stars, to make them easier for developers to access. A demo video is at https://youtu.be/MZqjDnJ8bEQ.

articles.insight: Web/APIインターフェースの認証・認可バイパスに関する典型的な脆弱性であり、ブラックボックス診断やDASTでの検出対象となり得ます。PLC制御を行うインターフェースに対して未認証で特権操作が実行できる状態は重大であり、ネットワーク分離だけでなく製品自体の根本的な認証機構の検証が必要です。診断業務では管理機能のエンドポイントに対するアクセス制御検証シナリオを強化する必要があります。
articles.importance_reason: 産業用制御環境において未認証での管理者権限奪取が可能となる極めて危険な脆弱性であるため。

articles.title: On Improving the Adoption, Usability, and Retention of Static Application Security Testing (SAST) Tools
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.21621v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: As the Internet connects more of the world, software vulnerabilities create growing security risks. Because software developers are responsible for building and maintaining secure applications, they rely on tools and techniques that help identify vulnerabilities early in development. Static Application Security Testing (SAST) tools analyze source code to identify potential security weaknesses before software is deployed. Although SAST can help developers address vulnerabilities proactively, these tools also present usability and adoption challenges. This thesis examines those challenges and explores ways to improve the adoption, usability, and continued use of SAST. First, a literature review of 89 research works related to SAST implementation and continued usage identifies recurring developer concerns, including false positives and other usability barriers that can reduce trust in SAST results. Second, the thesis presents a process for automating the execution of SAST tools and formatting their output so that findings are more meaningful and actionable to developers. A real-world use case evaluates an implementation of this process and gathers developer feedback. Participants reported satisfaction with several aspects of the process and indicated that it increased their willingness to use the SAST tool.
articles.title_ja: 静的アプリケーションセキュリティテスト（SAST）ツールの導入・有用性・継続利用の改善に関する研究
articles.summary_ja: ソフトウェアの脆弱性を早期に発見するためSASTツールが活用されていますが、誤検知や使い勝手の悪さが開発者の信頼低下や導入の障壁となっています。本論文では89件の関連研究の文献レビューを実施し、開発者の懸念事項を特定しました。さらに、SASTツールの実行自動化と出力フォーマットの改善プロセスを提案し、実際のユースケースを通じて開発者のツール利用意欲が向上することを確認しています。
articles.insight: SASTの導入や運用において、誤検知の多さや出力の分かりにくさが開発者のモチベーションや定着率を大きく左右します。静的診断ツールを導入・運用する際は、単にツールを導入するだけでなく、開発者が理解しやすい形式への出力整形や自動化プロセスの組込が不可欠です。診断ベンダーやセキュリティ担当者は、開発チームと協調したフィードバックループの構築を検討すべきです。
articles.importance_reason: SASTの導入障壁と実用的な改善プロセスを示しており、セキュア開発体制の構築に直結する知見であるため。

articles.title: Threat Landscape of Vibe Coding and the Road to Secure Autonomy
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.21822v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vibe coding is reshaping software development, enabling faster implementation and allowing individuals with limited programming experience to describe requirements in natural language while AI agents write, test, and deploy the code. As these agents evolve into autonomous systems that execute commands, manage dependencies, access cloud resources, and interact with other agents, their security risks extend beyond incorrect code to actions with direct consequences for software systems. Although research on these risks is expanding, it remains fragmented across areas including prompt injection, insecure code generation, supply-chain attacks, and human factors, with limited consensus on terminology, threat assumptions, and evaluation. This paper consolidates emerging research through the lens of the vibe coding workflow. We establish a reference architecture, characterise six levels of agent autonomy, and develop a threat model centred on five trust boundaries spanning developers, AI models, tools, cloud infrastructure, and the wider software ecosystem. Building on this foundation, we propose a taxonomy of twenty-one threats across nine classes. For each threat, we review the available evidence, assess proposed defences, and identify limitations. Our analysis highlights that risks increase with agents' operational authority, while most defences rely on model judgement and address isolated threats. Finally, we identify eleven research challenges, including enforceable limits on agent authority and shared benchmarks and methodologies for assessing vibe coding security.

articles.title_ja: バイブコーディングの脅威ランドスケープと安全な自律性へのロードマップ
articles.summary_ja: 自然言語による指示でAIエージェントがコード記述・テスト・デプロイを行う「バイブコーディング」がソフトウェア開発を変化させています。エージェントが自律的にコマンド実行やクラウド資源へのアクセスを行うようになるにつれて、セキュリティリスクは不適切なコード生成にとどまらず、システムに対する直接的な行動へと拡大しています。本論文では、ワークフローを中心とした参照アーキテクチャの確立、6段階のエージェント自律性の定義、5つの信頼境界に基づく脅威モデルを構築し、21の脅威に対する防御策と限界を整理しています。
articles.insight: AIエージェントの自律性が高まるにつれて、従来のコードの脆弱性だけでなく、エージェントの権限濫用やツール経由でのシステム破壊といった新たなリスクへの対策が必要です。自社でAIコーディング支援や自律型エージェントを導入する際には、エージェントに与える権限の制限や、モデルの判断だけに依存しない多層的な防御アーキテクチャの設計が求められます。ガバナンスとセキュリティの境界をどのように定義すべきか、早期の検討が不可欠です。
articles.importance_reason: AIエージェントの自律化に伴うセキュリティリスクと脅威モデルを包括的に分析しており、次世代のAIセキュリティ戦略に大きな示唆を与えるため。

articles.title: Adaptive Budget Allocation for Smart-Contract Fuzzing: Why Online Feedback Fails to Improve Vulnerability Triage
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.22430v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Smart-contract fuzzing campaigns share a finite budget and vary widely in the execution cost of a first correct-class vulnerability report. Using trace replay on 143 annotated and 350 bug-injected contracts, we test whether online feedback improves triage. At a mean budget of 100 executions per contract, uniform allocation reaches 72% and 70% of the respective clairvoyant optima. All eight online policies trail uniform on aggregate triage, as do the seven repeated on the bug-injected corpus. Five online signals yield ranking AUCs of 0.32-0.51 for imminent reports. Synthetic-oracle experiments show that sufficiently accurate detection-cost estimates recover more of the gap than detectability rankings. This motivates an offline probability-curve allocator that predicts first-report probabilities across budgets and allocates by predicted gain per execution. In a frozen evaluation on four fresh seeds per corpus, detection-budget AUC improves over uniform by 5.38% and 4.81% on the two source corpora and by 1.99-6.54% on three additional public benchmark subsets.

articles.title: X-LocVul: An Evidence-Propagation Audit of Cascaded C/C++ Vulnerability Detection, Localization, and Explanation
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.21626v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Developer-facing vulnerability analysis should link a function-level warning to a source location and a supported explanation. Cascaded systems can propagate weak evidence despite plausible components. We present X-LocVul, a measurement-first audit of a modular C/C++ detector-localizer-explainer pipeline combining UniXCoder, CodeT5, and Qwen2.5-Coder. We test whether evidence passed across stages is useful, merely source-resident, or misleading.
  Under duplication and temporal-leakage controls, UniXCoder has higher point estimates than CodeBERT, but true-CWE supervision is statistically indistinguishable from a shuffled-CWE control on PR-AUC, MCC, and vulnerable-class F1. Raw generated statements fail exact source matching in 90.83% of cases. Fuzzy projection reaches 83.79% Top-1 accuracy and exceeds semantic projection by 1.59 percentage points, although its advantage over raw ranking is not established. In a randomized, condition-label-masked two-rater evaluation of 50 paired cases, a predicted line improves evidence support, whereas a predicted CWE improves no endpoint. Oracle evidence improves evidence support (Holm-adjusted p=0.00453) and CWE consistency (p=3.49 x 10^-7), but not root-cause quality after correction (p=0.250); unsupported claims remain common. A chronological stress test retains ranking signal (ROC-AUC 0.782; PR-AUC 0.110), while the transferred threshold yields zero recall and F1.
  The contribution is not a state-of-the-art claim, but an auditable account of evidence construction, transfer, and consumption. It separates source residency from localization correctness, auxiliary labels from semantic supervision, and predicted evidence from useful evidence. Public E4 scores regenerate all 15 tests; missing manifests, final prompts, and profiler logs bound stronger reproducibility claims.
articles.title_ja: C/C++脆弱性検出・ローカライズ・説明生成パイプラインの監査
articles.summary_ja: モジュール型のC/C++脆弱性検出・ローカライズ・説明生成パイプライン（UniXCoder、CodeT5、Qwen2.5-Coderを組み合わせた構成）における証拠の伝播と品質を測定ベースで監査した。重複や時間的漏洩の制御下で評価を行った結果、CWEの教師あり学習はシャッフルされたCWEコントロールと統計的に区別がつかないことや、生成された文が正確なソースマッチに失敗するケースが多いことが示された。一方で、予測された行は証拠のサポートを改善するが、CWEの予測はエンドポイントを改善しないなどの知見が得られた。
articles.insight: AIを活用した脆弱性検出やコード解析ツールにおいて、出力される説明や分類ラベルの妥当性を厳しく検証する必要性を示している。単にAIモデルが出力したCWEや解説をうのみにせず、実際のソースコード上の位置情報や証拠の品質を評価に組み込むべきである。自動修正やSASTツールの評価において、誤った証拠の伝播を防ぐための検証プロセスの設計が重要となる。

articles.title: Experience: ENTRAP - An IaC Enterprise Cyber Range for Reproducible Security Assessment and Dataset Generation
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.20594v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An enterprise breach causes most of its damage after the perimeter is crossed. Once an attacker gains a foothold, they can move laterally to other hosts, take over the trusted services of the network, and encrypt the backups needed for recovery. Defenders, on the other hand, need to study this post-compromise stage, but they cannot rehearse it on a production enterprise network. Building such an enterprise network manually is time-consuming, and resetting it to its clean state between runs is still harder. As a result, security experiments are difficult to perform, compare and reproduce. We develop Enterprise Network Testbed for Reproducible Attack and Defense Practices (ENTRAP), an Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) cyber range that defines a fully segmented enterprise as version-controlled automation. ENTRAP uses Ansible, KVM/Libvirt, and Cloud-init to provision the environment and reset it to a clean state whenever necessary. The enterprise network includes several entities such as a gateway, an internal Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), DNS, DHCP, a backup server, a web server, and clients. On this network, a user can learn to assemble the entities, launch attacks, and write rules or defensive measures that harden its security. We launch three attacks: a Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS)-backed ransomware campaign, a Layer-2 DHCP starvation and rogue DHCP attack, and perimeter web exploitation. Each attack runs from a clean state, and ENTRAP acts as a reproducible generator of labeled attack datasets. Using the collected dataset, we train a Random Forest classifier for ransomware detection and present its evaluation results. We publicly release the codebase, collected logs, and datasets to facilitate further research.

articles.title: Use of Peer Code Review to Identify Potential Security Vulnerabilities in Open Source Software: A Systematic Literature Review
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.18568v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Context: Security vulnerabilities in OSS can have severe consequences. OSS project participants widely use peer code review to improve quality and prevent security flaws. However, despite mandatory reviews, OSS projects still contain vulnerabilities, highlighting the need to evaluate code review effectiveness for security. Objectives: This SLR synthesizes evidence on vulnerability types identified or missed, security practices, tool support, reviewer challenges, and factors that improve detection. Method: Searches of five digital libraries yielded 1,067 studies, of which 20 were included. Vulnerabilities were categorized using the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) framework. Results: Peer code reviews effectively detect localized, well-known vulnerabilities (e.g., buffer overruns, race conditions, crashes, XSS) but often miss subtle, complex, context-dependent issues (e.g., input validation weaknesses, access control weaknesses, resource lifecycle weaknesses). Effective security practices are associated with reviewer expertise, code familiarity, frequent small changes, and organizational support. Security analysis tools, especially Static Application Security Testing (SAST) tools, reduce reviewer effort and improve detection but cannot replace human judgment. Reviewers continue to face limitations in security knowledge, experience, time, and understanding of complex systems. Effectiveness improves through security training, domain expertise, contextual familiarity, formalized review processes, and supportive review environments. Conclusion: Peer code review contributes to OSS security but is insufficient on its own. Improving effectiveness requires structured review processes and checklists, security training, organizational incentives, and lightweight automated tool support to help reviewers detect subtle vulnerabilities while reinforcing secure development practices.

articles.title: TaintRadar: Semantic-Aware Taint-Style Vulnerability Detection via Augmented Code Property Graphs
articles.summary:
arXiv:2607.16456v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Despite significant advances, static vulnerability analysis suffers from three critical limitations: coarse sanitization modeling (treating validation as a binary barrier), database blindness (breaking taint tracking across persistence layers), and shallow object-oriented analysis (missing field-level and interprocedural data flows). These flaws stem from a common root cause: Code Property Graph (CPG)-based taint analyses lack a compositional semantic layer to jointly model sanitization, persistence, and object aliasing. Consequently, existing tools generate excessive false positives or miss critical attack paths entirely. To address these limitations, we present TaintRadar, an approach that systematically augments CPGs with three independent semantic analysis layers. First, vulnerability-typed sanitization computes node-level safety guarantees using transfer functions and context-sensitive parameter binding. Second, persistence-aware propagation integrates database schema constraints and query safety analysis to track multi-script attack paths traversing shared database states. Finally, object-aware reaching definitions combine calling and bounded variable alias contexts to precisely model object-field mutations across method boundaries. We evaluate TaintRadar on synthetic benchmarks and real-world systems. On the SARD benchmark, TaintRadar reduces false positives while maintaining 83 percent overall accuracy. Across 19 real-world PHP applications, it rediscovered most known CVEs and uncovered 30 confirmed zero-day vulnerabilities: 27 SQL injection and 3 stored XSS vulnerabilities. These vulnerabilities have been assigned CVE identifiers. Our results show that semantic-aware graph augmentation improves the precision, coverage, and practical utility of static taint analysis.

articles.title: Revisiting Re-executability: Coverage-Guided Symbolic Feedback to Improve Decompilation
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.18892v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When source code is unavailable, decompilation provides a source-level representation of a binary. However, code recovered by conventional or LLM-assisted decompilation may not preserve the original behavior of the binary. Recent approaches evaluate re-executability using fixed test suites, but passing these suites does not ensure behavioral preservation. We present SymDec, an LLM-assisted decompiled-code repair system that uses the original binary as a behavioral reference. SymDec uses coverage-guided symbolic execution to explore the I/O-level behavior of the original and recompiled binaries, and symbolic comparison to identify inputs that expose behavioral differences. These inputs are replayed on both binaries to confirm the differences, which are returned as structured feedback to guide subsequent LLM revisions. We evaluate SymDec on 120 functions from ExeBench and DecompileBench, compiled for x86-64 and ARM64 at optimization levels O0-O3, yielding 960 binary decompilation tasks. More than half of the tasks yield candidates that pass the supplied test suite and complete symbolic comparison without detected behavioral differences. Among candidates that pass all supplied tests, symbolic comparison exposes replay-confirmed behavioral differences in 4.5% of cases, showing that test-suite re-executability can miss behavioral discrepancies. Under the same input-generation budget, symbolic execution achieves higher mean line and branch coverage than black-box fuzzing. Symbolic feedback also improves the conventional metric, increasing the mean single-step test-pass rate from 90.1% to 93.3%. These results show that symbolic comparison provides stronger evidence of behavioral consistency than test-suite re-executability alone and supplies effective feedback for repairing decompiled code.
articles.title_ja: バイナリ逆コンパイルの正確性を高めるLLM支援のシンボリックフィードバックシステム「SymDec」

articles.title: Using machine learning approaches to classify false-positives generated by static analysis tools - An empirical study using small datasets
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.19079v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Static Code Analysis (SCA) tools are vital for software development to reduce the cost and time required for manual code reviews. It was established in our previous study that the best tools reported in the software engineering community return high false-positive and false-negative rates when used for code analysis. Several approaches have been taken in existing studies to identify false-positive alarms generated by SCA tools, in helping to enhance the utility of these tools. However, existing studies reveal several limitations, chiefly among which is the tendency to focus on a limited number of alarm types or failing to evaluate a large breadth of Machine-Learning (ML) techniques comprehensively. This study has addressed this opportunity. We identified the best Code Representation Learning (CRL) techniques and ML algorithms for identifying false-positives, where results show that performance outcomes vary based on the characteristics of the training datasets and the goal of the model building. Given the evidence established in this study, we recommend further investigations targeting specific configurations of advanced CRLs and ML Algorithms, including simple ML models.

articles.title: HackWorld: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Exploiting Web Application Vulnerabilities
articles.summary:
arXiv:2510.12200v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Web applications are prime targets for cyberattacks as gateways to critical services and sensitive data. Traditional penetration testing is costly and expertise-intensive, making it difficult to scale with the growing web ecosystem. While language model agents show promise in cybersecurity, modern web applications demand visual understanding, dynamic content handling, and multi-step interactions that only computer-use agents (CUAs) can perform. Yet, their ability to discover and exploit vulnerabilities through graphical interfaces remains largely unexplored. We present HackWorld, the first framework for systematically evaluating CUAs' capabilities to exploit web application vulnerabilities via visual interaction. Unlike sanitized benchmarks, HackWorld includes 36 real-world applications across 11 frameworks and 7 languages, featuring realistic flaws such as injection vulnerabilities, authentication bypasses, and unsafe input handling. Using a Capture-the-Flag (CTF) setup, it tests CUAs' capacity to identify and exploit these weaknesses while navigating complex web interfaces. Evaluation of state-of-the-art CUAs reveals concerning trends: exploitation rates below 12% and low cybersecurity awareness. CUAs often fail at multi-step attack planning and misuse security tools. These results expose the current limitations of CUAs in web security contexts and highlight opportunities for developing more security-aware agents capable of effective vulnerability detection and exploitation.

articles.title: A Governance Methodology Layer for AI-Assisted Software Development: Defect Taxonomy, Controlled Ablation, and a Test of Process-Over-Capability
articles.summary:
arXiv:2609.04218v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Autonomous coding agents produce output that passes syntactic checks -- compilation, type safety, CI -- at high velocity. Yet syntactic correctness does not imply semantic correctness: design boundaries, security invariants, and maintainability contracts remain structurally invisible to automated pipelines. This paper makes four contributions. First, we present a defect-class taxonomy grounded in five AI agent permission and governance modules, separating defects structurally detectable by static analysis from those requiring semantic review. Second, we describe a runtime-decoupled governance gate -- a file-based protocol that reads generator output and emits a structured verdict without API coupling, hence portable across generators. Third, we formalize methodology-as-code: expressing a verification protocol as a version-controlled, executable artifact whose two layers separate portable methodology from host automation. Fourth, we report a controlled ablation experiment (E-ablation, N=5 artifacts, 8-item independent ground truth) comparing harness-structured review against a token-matched unstructured prompt. The structured condition records 62% lenient recall against 50%, with 25% strict against 0%. A severity-grade differential reported earlier does not survive blind re-grading and is withdrawn (Sec. 6.6). An independent-session re-test with blind scoring does not replicate that contrast: the conditions differ by one strict hit in 24 (6/24 against 5/24), the structured aggregate again 25% and the unstructured 0% not recurring (Sec. 6.7). Both conditions miss document-quality defects identified by a human QA reviewer, indicating complementarity between structured AI review and human process inspection. A later pre-registered test varying model tier (184 runs) did not support process design as the dominant factor: under strict scoring the tier effect was larger (Sec. 6.8).

articles.title: Identifying and Mitigating API Misuse in Large Language Models
articles.summary:
arXiv:2503.22821v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: API misuse in code generated by large language models (LLMs) presents a serious and growing challenge in software development, as although LLMs demonstrate impressive code generation capabilities, their interactions with complex library APIs are often error-prone and can lead to software failures and vulnerabilities. In this paper, we conduct a large-scale study of API misuse patterns in LLM-generated code by analyzing both method selection and parameter usage across Python and Java, using three representative LLMs: StarCoder-7B, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, and GitHub Copilot. Based on extensive manual annotation of 3,209 method-level and 3,492 parameter-level misuses, we identify and categorize four recurring misuse types by building on and refining prior API misuse taxonomies. Our evaluation of the three LLMs reveals persistent challenges in API usage, particularly hallucination and intent misalignment. To address these issues, we propose Dr.Fix, an LLM-based automatic repair approach guided by our taxonomy, which improves repair accuracy compared to baseline prompting and existing repair methods, achieving gains of up to 38.4 BLEU and up to 72 more exact matches on benchmark datasets. This work offers important insights into the current limitations of LLMs in API usage and points to directions for improving automated misuse repair in code generation systems.

articles.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）が生成するコードにおけるAPIミューズ（誤用）は、ソフトウェアの障害や脆弱性を引き起こす深刻な課題となっている。本研究では、StarCoder-7B、Qwen2.5-Coder-7B、GitHub Copilotを用いたPythonとJavaのコード生成におけるAPIミューズパターンを大規模に調査した。3,209件のメソッドレベルおよび3,492件のパラメータレベルの誤用をアノテーションし、4つの再発する誤用タイプを特定・分類した。その上で、タクソノミーに導かれたLLMベースの自動修復アプローチ「Dr.Fix」を提案し、ベースラインプロンプトや既存手法と比較して修復精度が向上することを示している。

articles.title: Astraios: Parameter-Efficient Instruction Tuning Code Large Language Models
articles.summary:
arXiv:2401.00788v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The high cost of full-parameter fine-tuning (FFT) of Large Language Models (LLMs) has led to a series of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods. However, it remains unclear which methods provide the best cost-performance trade-off at different model scales. We introduce Astraios, a suite of 28 instruction-tuned OctoCoder models using 7 tuning methods and 4 model sizes up to 16 billion parameters. Through investigations across 5 tasks and 8 different datasets encompassing both code comprehension and code generation tasks, we find that FFT generally leads to the best downstream performance across all scales, and PEFT methods differ significantly in their efficacy based on the model scale. LoRA usually offers the most favorable trade-off between cost and performance. Further investigation into the effects of these methods on both model robustness and code security reveals that larger models tend to demonstrate reduced robustness and less security. At last, we explore the relationships among updated parameters, cross-entropy loss, and task performance. We find that the tuning effectiveness observed in small models generalizes well to larger models, and the validation loss in instruction tuning can be a reliable indicator of overall downstream performance.

articles.title_ja: Astraios：パラメータ効率の良い命令チューニングコード大規模言語モデルの研究
articles.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）のフルパラメータ微調整（FFT）の高コストを背景に、様々なパラメータ効率の良い微調整（PEFT）手法が提案されています。本研究では、4つのモデルサイズと7つのチューニング手法を用いた28のOctoCoderモデルからなる「Astraios」を導入し、コストと性能のトレードオフを調査しました。結果として、FFTが全スケールで最良の性能を示す一方で、LoRAがコストと性能の最も有利なトレードオフを提供することなどが明らかになりました。
articles.insight: コード生成・理解向けLLMのファインチューニング手法選択において、コストとパフォーマンスのバランスを見極めるための重要な指標を提供しています。セキュリティ診断や自動修正機能を持つAIエージェントの開発・導入時、モデルの規模とPEFT手法がセキュリティや堅牢性に与える影響を評価する際の参考になります。

articles.title: Adversarial Attacks on Downstream Weather Forecasting Models: Application to Tropical Cyclone Trajectory Prediction
articles.summary:
arXiv:2510.10140v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Deep learning-based weather forecasting (DLWF) models leverage past weather observations to generate future forecasts, supporting a wide range of downstream applications, including tropical cyclone (TC) prediction. In this paper, we investigate the vulnerability of these models to adversarial attacks, where subtle perturbations to upstream forecasts can alter downstream TC trajectory predictions. Crafting perturbed inputs to steer downstream outputs toward attacker-specified trajectories is a challenging problem for several reasons. First, conventional TC detection systems are opaque, non-differentiable black boxes, making standard gradient-based attacks infeasible. Second, the extreme rarity of TC events leads to a severe class imbalance problem, making it difficult to develop attack methods that produce realistic-looking cyclone paths aligned with target trajectories. To overcome these limitations, we propose Cyc-Attack, a novel method for perturbing the forecasts of DLWF models to generate adversarial trajectories. The proposed method uses a differentiable surrogate model to approximate the TC detector's output, enabling the application of gradient-based attacks. Cyc-Attack also employs a skewness-aware loss function with a kernel dilation strategy to address the severe class imbalance problem. Distance-based gradient weighting and regularization strategies are also introduced to constrain perturbations to eliminate unrealistic-looking TC paths. Our experiments show that Cyc-Attack achieves a higher true positive rate in matching the target trajectories, along with lower false alarm rates and stealthier perturbations than conventional attack methods. We further demonstrate that the adversarial upstream forecasts generated by Cyc-Attack can be leveraged as initial guidance to train an end-to-end model for learning adversarial input samples that would induce target trajectories.
articles.title_ja: 深層学習気象予測モデルに対する敵対的攻撃手法「Cyc-Attack」の提案
articles.summary_ja: 深層学習ベースの気象予測（DLWF）モデルは熱帯低気圧（TC）の進路予測など下流アプリケーションを支援していますが、上流予測への微小な摂動により下流の進路予測が改ざんされる脆弱性が研究されました。従来のTC検出系は微分不可能かつデータ不均衡が極端なため攻撃が困難でしたが、微分可能な代理モデルと不均衡対応損失関数を用いた新手法「Cyc-Attack」が提案されました。実験では、従来手法よりも高い適合率、低い誤警報率、高い隠密性で標的の進路を偽装できることが示されました。
articles.insight: AIモデルのパイプラインにおいて上流データへのわずかな入力摂動が下流の意思決定を大きく歪めるリスクを実証した研究であり、物理インフラや予測系AIのセキュリティ評価において敵対的入力検証の重要性を示唆しています。モデルの堅牢性検証では、ブラックボックスな後続システムに対しても代理モデルを用いた勾配近似攻撃が成立することを前提にしたテスト設計が必要です。AIモデルのライフサイクルにおいて、推論パイプライン全体の入出力整合性を検証する監査フレームワークの設計が求められます。
articles.importance_reason: ブラックボックスな下流AIシステムに対しても代理モデルを用いて入力摂動による出力操作が成立することを示した学術的研究であるため。

business.evidence: arXivの学術論文による研究提案（arXiv:2510.10140v3）であり、悪用報告やインシデントの記述はない。

attack.service_implication: AIモデルの堅牢性診断において、非微分可能なシステムに対するサロゲートモデルを用いた敵対的摂動試験の適用可能性を検討する

articles.insight: インフラの中核を担うエンタープライズストレージにおけるクリティカルな脆弱性であり、露出している管理インターフェースやAPIの存在確認と迅速なパッチ管理が強く求められます。脆弱性診断の実務においては、外部公開資産だけでなく内部ネットワークの境界診断や構成監査を通じて未適用の重要ストレージアプライアンスを正確に識別することが急務です。修正パッチ適用後の回帰テストやファームウェア更新手順をあらかじめ運用設計に組み込むことが重要となります。
articles.importance_reason: 基幹インフラストレージ製品におけるクリティカル判定の脆弱性群であり、迅速な評価と緩和が求められるため。

articles.summary: The FBI is warning that hackers are using an AI-powered penetration testing framework called ARTEX to automate cyberattacks against organizations worldwide, including a recent ConnectWise supply-chain breach that compromised Microsoft 365 customer environments. [...]
articles.title_ja: FBI、AIペネトレーションテストツール「ARTEX」を悪用したサイバー攻撃に警告
articles.summary_ja: FBIは、ARTEXと呼ばれるAI搭載ペネトレーションテストフレームワークが世界的なサイバー攻撃の自動化に悪用されているとして警告を発しました。このツールは、Microsoft 365顧客環境が侵害された最近のConnectWiseサプライチェーン侵害などにも利用されたとされています。攻撃者はAIを活用して侵入および侵害活動を高速化・自動化しています。
articles.insight: AI支援型ペネトレーションテストツールが実攻撃へ転用されている事実は、攻撃者の偵察や侵入のサイクルが短縮している可能性を示唆します。防御側や診断サービス提供者は、従来の定期的な診断だけでなく、継続的な露出管理や自動化された検証手法を取り入れる必要があります。AIによる自動攻撃シナリオに対して、現在のID・アクセス管理や多要素認証の設計が十分機能するかは検証すべき論点です。
articles.importance_reason: AIツールを悪用した自動化攻撃がサプライチェーン侵害などの実被害に利用されているとFBIが警告しており影響が大きいため。

articles.title: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back to Life After a 24-Hour Outage
articles.summary: The company says a bad update—not a cyberattack or AI—caused its servers around the world to crash.
articles.title_ja: Microsoft 365が24時間の大規模障害から復旧、原因はアップデートの不具合
articles.summary_ja: Microsoft 365のサービスが世界規模で24時間にわたり停止した後、復旧に向かいました。マイクロソフト社は、今回の世界的なサーバー障害の原因はサイバー攻撃やAIによるものではなく、不具合を含む不良アップデート（bad update）によるものと説明しています。インフラ更新における検証プロセスの課題が改めて示されました。
articles.insight: サイバー攻撃や外部脅威でなくとも、ソフトウェア更新起因で世界規模のサービス停止が発生し得ることを示す事例です。脆弱性修正パッチや構成変更を本番適用する際のテストパイプラインやカナリアリリースの重要性が再認識されます。依存するSaaSの障害発生時における事業継続計画やBCP設計の妥当性が問われます。
articles.importance_reason: 基盤的クラウドサービスの停止が広範囲に影響を与え、変更管理・更新の安全性検証における重要な教訓となるため。

articles.title: PostgreSQL Patches 52 Flaws, Including 22-Year-Old Bug Enabling Authenticated RCE
articles.summary:
A type confusion flaw in PostgreSQL lets a database user who can create objects run code on the server. Updates released yesterday fix it, along with 51 other security flaws. Full protection from this flaw also requires rebuilding any C-language extensions installed on the server.

The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-6460, has a CVSS score of 8.8. Any code run this way has the rights of the operating
articles.title_ja: PostgreSQL、認証済みRCEにつながる長年のバグを含む52件の脆弱性を修正
articles.summary_ja: PostgreSQLにおいて、オブジェクト作成権限を持つユーザーがサーバー上でコード実行可能となる型混乱の脆弱性（CVE-2026-6460、CVSS 8.8）が修正されました。今回のアップデートでは計52件の脆弱性が修正されており、中には22年間にわたり存在していた欠陥も含まれます。完全な修正にはパッチ適用だけでなく、インストールされているC言語拡張の再ビルドが必要です。
articles.insight: データベースアカウントを用いた認証済みRCE脆弱性であり、権限昇格対策や内部脅威防御の観点で極めて重要です。静的診断やDAST単独では拡張モジュール起因の型混乱を網羅しにくいため、構成監査やパッチ管理プロセスの再確認が必要です。C言語拡張の再コンパイルが必須要件となっており、再診断や修正プロセスの運用負荷と機能維持の検証が求められます。
articles.importance_reason: 極めて広く利用されているPostgreSQLにおける高深刻度のRCE脆弱性であり、広範なシステムに影響するため。

articles.title_ja: 週次ニュース概括：OpenAI Codexバックドアリスク、モデル重みのバックドア、車載機器侵害など

articles.title_ja: AIエージェントの暴走・不正操作への停止制御とアイデンティティ管理の課題

articles.title: VU#644655: TightVNC and UltraVNC Viewer contains a heap-based buffer overflow
articles.summary:
Overview

A heap-based buffer overflow exists in the Tight JPEG decoding component of the TightVNC Windows Viewer version 1.3.10 and affected UltraVNC Windows Viewers. An attacker controlling a malicious VNC server can trigger memory corruption by sending a specially crafted screen update. Successful exploitation can crash the viewer and may allow arbitrary code execution, although only denial of service conditions were demonstrated during testing.

articles.insight: VNCビューアなどのリモートデスクトップクライアントにおける画像・画面デコード処理の脆弱性は、クライアント側からの接続時に標的型攻撃の踏み台となるリスクがある。SCAやソースコード診断においてサードパーティライブラリのデコード処理の安全性を確認することが重要である。

articles.title: MobileProbe: Adaptive Security Evaluation of Mobile Agents via Trajectory-Aware Injection
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.16693v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mobile GUI agents read the screen of a phone and operate apps on a user's behalf to complete multi-step tasks such as online shopping or messaging. Because the agent acts on whatever the screen shows, an attacker can embed malicious instructions into ordinary UI content and redirect its actions. We refer to this threat as environmental injection attack (EIA). Existing benchmarks measure this risk by pinning hand-crafted payloads to a fixed step of a fixed task. This approach faces two limitations. First, each payload is bound to one task in one app and does not transfer without manual redesign. Second, agents given the same task may follow different routes, so an agent that never reaches the injected page is recorded as safe without being tested. This insufficient test coverage can cause fixed-point benchmarks to underestimate the security risk of deployed mobile agents.
  In this work, we propose MobileProbe, a trajectory-aware red-teaming framework that evaluates mobile agents adaptively. MobileProbe discovers attacker-controllable content surfaces through automated pentesting, localizes vulnerable decision points along the agent's trajectory, and iteratively refines context-aware payloads through a surrogate-filtered evolutionary loop. We construct a benchmark of 83 long-horizon attack instances spanning 12 mobile applications. Each is annotated with a Confidentiality, Integrity, or Availability (CIA) attack goal to cover the principal categories of security threats facing mobile agents. On three representative agent architectures, MobileProbe attains higher attack success rates than human-written, zero-shot LLM, and prior automated red-teaming baselines adapted to the mobile domain. MobileProbe can serve as a pre-deployment auditing tool to systematically uncover vulnerabilities and inform security hardening of mobile agents.

articles.title: GHA-SmellFix: Taking Action with Agentic LLMs for Detecting and Refactoring GitHub Actions Workflow Smells
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.14963v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Continuous integration and continuous delivery workflows are key artifacts in software projects. In GitHub Actions, they encode build, test, release, deployment, and security automation in YAML. These workflows contain configuration smells affecting security, reliability, maintainability, or operational stability. Existing approaches are mostly rule-based, with rules hard to create and evolve, and typically report findings without fixes. Agentic LLM pipelines can combine contextual detection, transformation selection, and patch generation. Specialized agents can gate refactoring on positive detection verdicts, potentially avoiding unnecessary changes, but it is unclear whether decomposition improves effectiveness or mainly changes overhead. We present GHA-SmellFix, an agentic LLM pipeline for detecting and refactoring GitHub Actions workflow smells. We compare two designs: Joint, where one agent detects and refactors, and Decomposed, where separate agents detect and then refactor. We operationalize 19 smells from an existing catalog with explicit detection criteria, refactoring expectations, exclusion rules, and safety checks, and curate a ground truth of 1,710 (workflow, smell) pairs. We evaluate the designs with four LLMs (GPT-5.4-nano, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Claude Haiku 4.5, and DeepSeek V4 Flash) on 570 sampled pairs. Results show that decomposition does not universally improve patch quality; its main benefit is controlling when patch generation is attempted. It helps models prone to missing smells and can reduce overhead by gating patches. Once a smell is correctly detected, clean refactoring is generally effective, making detection the main end-to-end bottleneck. However, false positives can trigger unnecessary edits to execution-relevant constructs. Practical CI/CD agents thus need reliable abstention and construct-aware validation alongside patch generation.

articles.title: Preserve the Vulnerability, Break the Alert: Testing the Robustness of CodeQL Taint Tracking with Natural Rewrites
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.17123v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Static application security testing (SAST) tools such as CodeQL serve as security gates in continuous integration and code review, and a gate is also read in reverse. When a previously reported alert disappears after a change, developers and the tools around them often take the vulnerability to be gone. That inference holds only if the analyzer is robust to changes that keep the vulnerability. We test this robustness for CodeQL's JavaScript taint tracking with natural, vulnerability-preserving rewrites. A large language model, given only the alert CodeQL exposes and no knowledge of its implementation, rewrites one function along a reported flow as a plausible maintenance change, and we verify by manual audit and controlled experiments that the flaw survives and the alert does not. On 172 flows that CodeQL detects in real npm vulnerabilities, three rewrites per flow silence 26.2% of them, at about USD 0.51 per silenced flow. The same generator, asked only to refactor the same functions with no knowledge of the alert, silences none of them. Every silencing rewrite traces to one of seven gaps at the library-modeling boundary, and 64 of the 70 rewrites cross a gap inside an API CodeQL already models. The largest is the WHATWG URL constructor, which propagates taint to a URL's query components but not to its pathname. The boundary is not specific to CodeQL. 74% of the silencing rewrites also silence an independently built taint analyzer, and 53% escape three analyzers combined. A disappearing alert after an ordinary-looking change is therefore weak evidence that a vulnerability has been fixed, the gaps point SAST developers to narrow and concrete repair targets, and robustness to natural rewrites belongs alongside detection rate in how taint analyzers are evaluated.
articles.title_ja: 脆弱性を維持したままアラートを沈黙させる：自然な書き換えによるCodeQL汚染追跡の堅牢性検証
articles.summary_ja: 静的アプリケーションセキュリティテスト（SAST）において、修正後にアラートが消えることは脆弱性が解消されたことを意味するとみなされがちである。本研究では、CodeQLのJavaScript汚染追跡に対し、脆弱性を維持したまま自然な保守的書き換えを行う手法を検証した。LLMを用いて関数を書き換えたところ、検出された現実のnpm脆弱性のうち26.2%のアラートが沈黙した。このアラートの消失は脆弱性の修正を意味しないため、検出率だけでなく書き換えに対する堅牢性も評価指標に含めるべきである。

articles.title: Beyond the Diff - VulSpot: A Vulnerability Dataset Where No Vulnerability Goes Unlocalized
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.15737v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A vulnerability detector is only as trustworthy as the benchmark that scores it, and today's real-world datasets tend to flatter detectors. They are often built once and never refreshed, so they quickly miss new vulnerabilities, their labels are either noisy or heavily filtered, and their random splits let models train on near-copies of test code and on future vulnerabilities. Above all, when a fix only adds code, such as a missing NULL check, they do not point at where the vulnerability was, preventing detectors from learning to localize some of the most common C/C++ weaknesses. We present VulSpot, a living benchmark for detecting, classifying, and localizing vulnerabilities, with over 500k functions in 21 languages from 24k registered CVEs, including over 15k vulnerable C/C++ functions. By linking the code added by a patch to the existing statement it protects, VulSpot locates the vulnerability in 99.3\% of the functions that previous diff-based datasets used to leave without a location. Rather than discarding uncertain labels, it tells users how reliable each one is, and it comes with leak-free splits, complementary code context, and hierarchical CWE labels. An automated pipeline refreshes VulSpot every month, so that each release brings vulnerabilities no model has seen yet.

articles.title: Pre-QED: Environment Specifications for Agentic Verification
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.15207v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents are making formal verification practical at scale. Recently, many attempts have raised this as an enticing possibility. However, formal verification at scale is only meaningful if deep formal specifications capturing functionality are available for checking. Unfortunately, recent works seek to bypass this issue by using shallow specifications devised for purposes other than verification. OSS-Verify from Anthropic and Theorem, for example, reuses the fuzz harnesses of open-source libraries as specifications and has an agent prove that each harness never crashes. However, a fuzz harness follows a single sequence of API calls under a single calling context, so the resulting proof covers one usage scenario rather than the library.
  We argue that the bottleneck of agentic verification has shifted from how to prove to what to prove. Before zooming into verification at scale, we need deep environment specifications to prove, which is why we call our effort Pre-QED. We propose verification harnesses, executable harnesses that model all legal usages of an API, so that a proof about the harness is a proof about every well-behaved client. To construct them, we use an agentic workflow that extracts the API's usage contract from code / documentation, and uses Linear-time Temporal Logic (LTL) to rule out illegal call orders. We identify the challenges in proving verification harnesses and release our harnesses open-source as challenges for the community. The overarching vision is that verifying an open-source library should become as routine as fuzzing it, with a guarantee that covers every well-behaved client rather than a single scenario like a fuzzing harness.
articles.title_ja: Pre-QED：LLMエージェントによる形式手法検証のための環境仕様ハーネス生成

articles.title: The Import Tax: A Longitudinal Measurement of Startup Cost in the Python Ecosystem
articles.summary:
arXiv:2609.02753v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Python programs pay for their imports at every process start, a cost that is invisible in steady-state benchmarks but dominant for command-line tools, test workers, and serverless cold starts. Python 3.15 adds explicit lazy imports (PEP 810) on largely anecdotal evidence. We measure the import cost of the 500 most-downloaded PyPI packages, every quarterly release since mid-2021, under six CPython versions (3.9-3.14) on two platforms (Apple M5/macOS and Intel Xeon/Linux), 66,816 cells in all, with targeted experiments that isolate individual effects. Values are for macOS (Linux in parentheses). Import cost is heavily skewed (median 12.3 ms, 99th percentile 400 ms). Among packages that import in more than 2 ms, namespace distributions excluded, the median package spends 68% of its import time in the standard library (68% on Linux with the interpreter on local storage, 79% on network storage). Precompiling bytecode removes almost all of the cold-start penalty on Linux and 92% of it for the median package on macOS, but only a third of the summed macOS penalty: packages with native libraries pay a security assessment of each library that the system has not seen before, again in every fresh environment. A package's own import code grows by a median 4.0% (5.0%) per year; installing each release with the dependencies of its time changes its trend by a median of only 0.15 (0.35) percentage points (CPython 3.9). CPython 3.14 runs package code faster than 3.9 but imports more and slower standard-library modules, a net 1.16x (1.07x) slowdown. Submodules that dependents import beyond the top level add nothing for the median package and at most 11.7 (49.5) ms for nine packages in ten. On CPython 3.15, global lazy mode cuts the imports that dependents perform to 0.41x (0.39x) of their cost, and 38 of 461 packages fail under it, many only on first use of a name. Harness, code, and dataset are public.

articles.title: BypassGym: A Benchmark for Evaluating AI Agents' Endpoint Defense Evasion Capabilities
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.13684v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Artificial intelligence agents increasingly automate cybersecurity tasks, including offensive operations. Frequent attacks across the web make endpoint detection and response (EDR) a critical defense, but whether AI agents can evade it remains unclear. Benchmarks evaluate the offensive capabilities of large language model (LLM) agents in areas such as penetration testing and vulnerability discovery. One important capability that these benchmarks do not address is defense evasion, specifically whether an agent can develop a program that executes a payload without being blocked or terminated by a deployed EDR. We introduce BypassGym, to our knowledge the first benchmark to systematically evaluate this capability on real endpoints. Given command-and-control (C2) shellcode, an agent must generate and compile a loader that executes the payload without being blocked or terminated. A supplementary evasion knowledge skill provides domain knowledge and supports comparisons with and without this input. BypassGym is built on Proxmox VE(PVE), so the evaluation environment runs real Windows systems and EDR products inside virtual machines and returns structured detection feedback to the agent. We evaluate 5 lightweight model backends against 6 EDR products and 3 payloads, and find that even these simple models generate successful submissions, with DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash reaching 17/18 successful runs and Bitdefender allowing only 5 of 15 runs to pass. These results provide a systematic measurement of current AI agents' endpoint defense evasion capabilities and identify areas for defenders to investigate.
engineering_topics: 評価基盤・データセット

articles.insight: AIエージェントが実環境のEDR回避ローダーを生成可能であることが実験的に示された。ペネトレーションテストやレッドチーム業務におけるAI活用が進む一方で、攻撃者によるEDR回避の自動化リスクが現実味を帯びている。EDRベンダーおよび監視運用設計者は、AIが試行錯誤によって生成するシグネチャ・動的検知回避パターンをいかに捕捉するかという課題に直面している。

articles.title: Code-Grounded Agentic Explanations for Static Analysis Vulnerability Findings
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.13041v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Static application security testing (SAST) tools surface vulnerabilities early and their verdicts are rule-based and auditable. Yet developers routinely dismiss findings they cannot interpret. Large language models can supply the missing explanation, but designs that also hand the model the detection give up the auditability that makes static analysis defensible. We keep detection with the analyser and give the model only the explaining. A preliminary user study with 20 participants and a workshop with 19 practitioners yielded five requirements. Guided by these we redesigned SAFE, an open-source IntelliJ IDEA plugin that explains findings from any analyser reporting in the Static Analysis Results Interchange Format. It tiers explanations by demand, ties them to the reported data flow, and replaces the single-prompt backend with an agent that must consult the repository and the rule that fired before answering. A within-subjects crossover experiment with 24 participants compared the redesign against its predecessor. Perceived usability rose from 77.3 to 85.0 on the System Usability Scale. Actionability gained most among the explanation-quality items, the aspect both earlier studies flagged as weakest, and the odds of a correct remediation were 2.6 times higher. Triage accuracy and time per finding were indistinguishable, which we read as uninformative rather than as equivalence. Trust was the one measure that did not move, and the closing interviews indicate that grounding made findings easier to understand rather than easier to believe. Participants also drew a boundary no requirement anticipated, wanting the tool to find and explain while they judge and apply.
articles.title_ja: 静的解析脆弱性検知結果に対するコード準拠型AIエージェントによる解説支援
articles.summary_ja: 静的解析（SAST）ツールは網羅的かつ監査可能な検知を提供するが、開発者が検知結果の意味を解釈できず却下する課題が存在する。本研究では検知自体は既存アナライザーに維持したまま、SARIF形式の検知結果に対してコードリポジトリや発火ルールを参照して段階的に解説するIntelliJ IDEAプラグイン「SAFE」を設計した。被験者実験の結果、ユーザビリティやアクション性が向上し、修正の正答オッズが2.6倍に改善された一方、検知結果に対する信頼度そのものは変化しなかった。
articles.insight: AIエージェントを脆弱性の独自検知ではなく「静的解析結果の文脈依存的な解説と修正支援」に限定することで、監査可能性を維持しつつ開発者の修正精度を大きく引き上げられる実証例である。トリアージ時間や精度自体は大きく変わらない点、および開発者が「判断と適用は人間が行う」という境界を望んでいる点は、AI活用診断プラットフォーム設計における重要な示唆となる。
articles.importance_reason: SASTの監査性を損なわずにAIによる解説・修正ガイダンスを組み込むアーキテクチャと効果測定を示したため。

articles.title: How Well Do SAST Tools Work Across Languages? An Empirical Study Using OCPP Implementations
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.14362v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As electric vehicle (EV) adoption accelerates globally, securing electric vehicle charging station (EVCS) software becomes increasingly critical. The Open Charge Point Protocol (OCPP), widely adopted for EVCS management, places significant responsibility on developers to securely implement specifications that are subject to multiple interpretations. The variety of OCPP implementations across different programming languages provides a unique opportunity to evaluate security tooling in a real-world, multi-language context where implementation variability may introduce vulnerabilities. This study provides the first empirical evaluation of Static Application Security Testing (SAST) tool performance across multiple programming languages using OCPP implementations as a real-world test corpus. We applied both comprehensive multi-language tools (SonarQube and Semgrep) and language-specific analyzers to twelve OCPP 1.6 implementations--each written in a distinct programming language--to examine how detection patterns vary across language ecosystems. Total issues ranged from just two in Rust to 1,689 in Java. Mature programming languages like Java yielded substantially more findings than newer languages like Rust, likely because established languages have more developed SAST tool ecosystems rather than inherently worse code quality. These results suggest that developers should consider available SAST tooling when selecting implementation languages for security critical systems.
articles.title_ja: 言語間におけるSASTツールの性能差：OCPP実装を用いた実証研究
articles.summary_ja: EV充電スタンド管理プロトコルであるOCPPの実装は多様なプログラミング言語で行われており、実装依存の解釈による脆弱性リスクが懸念されている。本研究は12種類のプログラミング言語で書かれたOCPP 1.6実装をコーパスとし、SonarQubeやSemgrep等の複数言語対応ツールおよび言語固有アナライザーの検出状況を実証評価した。その結果、検出された問題数はRustの2件からJavaの1,689件まで大きな開きがあり、言語ごとのSASTエコシステムの成熟度が検出数に大きく影響していることが示された。
articles.insight: ソースコード診断において、検出された脆弱性・課題の多寡がコード自体の安全性の差異ではなく、単に対象言語のSASTエコシステムの成熟度に依存している可能性を明確に示している。セキュリティ要件が厳しいシステムの実装言語選定や、マルチ言語環境でのExposure管理・脆弱性診断の基準設計において、ツール側のカバレッジの限界を把握しておく必要性を示唆する。
articles.importance_reason: 同一プロトコル実装に対するマルチ言語SAST比較を通じ、ツール検出能力と言語エコシステム成熟度の相関を実証したため。

articles.title: An Empirical Study on CVE-based Vulnerabilities Propagation from one System to another System (IntraProject vs InterProject)
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.14164v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vulnerabilities in applications, including browsers, media players, online services and document readers, etc. are often exploited and cause a serious damage. The vulnerabilities could exist in your system maybe because of some coding errors, design oversights, outdated software, AI generated codes or maybe transferred from another system during development (e.g., code clones). The propagation of software vulnerabilities is a critical concern in cybersecurity. This study examines the root cause problem of vulnerabilities propagation with experiments. We analyzed the propagation of CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) based vulnerabilities within and between different software projects (IntraProject vs. InterProject). We performed several experiments on CVE based vulnerability dataset (retrieved from NVD source) by using our vulnerability detection tool (SQVDT). In the results, we discovered similar patterns of vulnerable code in several very famous recently used software, including latest version of Linux, Android operating systems, and in thousands of open source projects available on GitHub. We found several very high severity level (CVSS) vulnerabilities that propagated from one system to another system, just because of copy/paste (reuse) the code. Furthermore, we performed an empirical evaluation and verification of these vulnerable patterns that propagated to other systems by also considering the frequency of their propagation. Finlay, we recommended the impact of these vulnerabilities propagation on the interconnected systems.
engineering_topics: 生成コードの安全性評価

articles.title_ja: コード複製によるCVE脆弱性のシステム間伝播に関する実証研究
articles.summary_ja: 本論文は、同一プロジェクト内および異なるプロジェクト間におけるコード再利用（コピペ等）によるCVE脆弱性の伝播メカニズムを実証的に調査した研究である。著者らは脆弱性検出ツールSQVDTを用い、NVDから取得したCVEデータセットに基づき大規模な実験を実施した。その結果、LinuxやAndroidの最新バージョン、およびGitHub上の数千のオープンソースプロジェクトにおいて、コード再利用に起因する重大な脆弱性パターンの伝播が確認された。
articles.insight: 単一のライブラリ依存関係だけでなく、コードクローンによる脆弱性の混入はSCAツールのみでは追跡が困難である。ソースコード診断（SAST）やリポジトリ監査において、既知のCVEパターンに基づく静的マッチングやクローン検出の導入が検討課題となる。開発組織がAI生成コードや外部コードをコピー＆ペーストする運用に対し、CI/CDパイプラインでの検証基盤をどう構築すべきかが問われる。
articles.importance_reason: LinuxやAndroidを含む広範なオープンソースエコシステムにコード再利用経由で重大な脆弱性が拡散している事実を実証しているため。

articles.title_ja: 米当局、Cisco・Chromium・Barracudaなど悪用確認済みの脆弱性6件に注意喚起
articles.summary_ja: 米サイバーセキュリティ当局は、「Cisco BroadWorks」や「Chromium」などに存在する脆弱性6件が実際のサイバー攻撃において悪用されているとして注意喚起を実施した。特にBarracuda Networks製品の脆弱性に関しては、被害拡大を防ぐため早急な対応が必要とされている。影響を受けるシステムに対するパッチ適用と露出資産の把握が求められる。
articles.insight: 公認された悪用実績（KEV相当）を持つ製品脆弱性に対しては、従来の定期診断スケジュールを待たずに迅速なExposure管理と緊急対応が要求される。国内組織においても同一製品が境界防御やネットワーク基盤に導入されているケースがあり、資産インベントリと照合した緊急診断が欠かせない。優先順位付けにおいて、当局の悪用確認リストをトリアージトリガーとして組み込めているかが問われる。
articles.importance_reason: 複数の主要ネットワークおよびクライアント製品における既知の悪用事実に基づく米当局の緊急注意喚起であるため。

business.evidence: 米当局が悪用確認済みとして6件の脆弱性（Cisco BroadWorks、Chromium、Barracuda製品等）を注意喚起し、早急な対応を要請。

attack.service_implication: 脆弱性管理・診断サービスにおいて、悪用確認済み資産を即座に特定・通知する緊急検知フローの有効性を再点検する。
