articles.title: CyberBinGym: Can AI Agents Turn Binary Patches into Real Exploits?
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.10723v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Security fixes usually reach users as compiled updates, but deployment delays leave unpatched systems exposed. During this window, comparing patched and unpatched binaries can reveal how to exploit a vulnerability, turning a defensive update into actionable information for attackers. Existing benchmarks do not measure this capability: they expose source code, rely on human-crafted challenges, or evaluate binary comprehension without requiring exploitation. We introduce CyberBinGym, a benchmark containing 100 tasks derived from real vulnerabilities in 53 widely used projects, spanning six vulnerability families and three levels of analysis complexity. Agents receive stripped vulnerable and patched binaries without source code or vulnerability information, and must combine static and dynamic analysis to recover and exploit the vulnerability. Evaluation separately measures vulnerability recovery through differential crash testing and end-to-end exploitation through flag retrieval, with trajectory audits to reject reward hacking. The strongest evaluated agent recovers the target vulnerability in 88% of tasks and exploits it in 20%. Providing the patched binary raises its exploit rate from 10% to 25% on a matched 20-task subset; with standard binary hardening enabled, it still exploits two of its 20 previously successful tasks. These results demonstrate that current agents can turn released binary patches into working exploits in a controlled setting, although exploitation remains unreliable. These capabilities lower the barriers to targeting unpatched software and compress defenders' effective response window, increasing the urgency of timely patch deployment.

articles.title: RoCoMark: Robust Code Watermarking Against LLM-Based Functionality-Preserving Rewriting Attacks
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.11399v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) present significant challenges to source tracing of generated code, as LLM rewriting can substantially alter the syntactic and structural characteristics of watermarked code. However, existing watermarking methods often suffer severe performance degradation under LLM-based functionality-preserving rewriting attacks. We attribute this vulnerability not merely to the intensity of rewriting, but to a fundamental distribution mismatch between the perturbations encountered during watermark training and the global, non-deterministic rewriting behaviors induced by LLMs. In order to deal with this challenge, we propose RoCoMark, a Robust Code waterMarking framework that explicitly learns and adapts to LLM rewriting behaviors. RoCoMark is a multi-round minimax game between the watermark embedder and LLM rewriter. In each round, the embedder first learns threat profiling from LLM-rewritten code by optimizing the watermark encoder through contrastive learning and knowledge distillation while mitigating catastrophic representation drift. Then the embedder improves strategies by optimizing the watermark encoder and extractor simultaneously. Finally, an adaptive attack-evolution mechanism based on Reflexion and short- and long-term memory pools is applied, enabling continuous interaction between the watermark embedder and evolving rewriting strategies. This iterative attacker-defender process progressively improves the robustness of the watermark against diverse and previously unseen LLM rewriting behaviors. Extensive experiments on four typical benchmarks, under attacks generated by five LLMs, show the effectiveness of RoCoMark. RoCoMark achieves an average detection AUROC of 74.2% and a Rewrite BitACC of 75.3%, while maintaining a code functionality pass rate above 99.7%.

articles.title: Coding Agents Propagate Vulnerabilities in Code Bases
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.11455v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based coding agents are widely used to develop critical production software. Even though coding agents are known to occasionally write vulnerable code, there has not been any investigation into how code base vulnerabilities evolve over time under coding agent contributions. In this work, we close this gap by investigating whether and how vulnerabilities in existing code lead coding agents to introduce similar vulnerabilities in the code they write. We first evaluate coding agents on 96 tasks that require implementing a new backend application in a repository where other applications already exist. Second, we investigate repository-level code generation on 20 pairs of tasks in real C/C++ projects. In each task, the agent is asked to complete code critical to memory safety. We find that in both settings, insecure existing code leads to agents writing vulnerable code more often. In backend generation, insecure neighbors reduce the share of correct and secure implementations by 3.4% on average, and in C/C++ repository-level coding, the average gap between secure and insecure contexts reaches 35.4%. Prompting to follow existing code-style or to be careful about security increases, respectively decreases, how strongly agents propagate vulnerabilities, but neither stops them. When asked to explain their implementation choices, coding agents attribute them to following another code site in 76.5% of cases, even though they recognize the introduced vulnerability in 69.9% of cases. These findings show that agents use existing vulnerabilities as templates for new ones indiscriminatorily, turning each contribution into an opportunity to introduce more vulnerabilities. As such, as agents write a growing share of production code under decreasing human review, code bases can increasingly degrade in security if security vulnerabilities are not thoroughly fixed continuously.
engineering_topics: 生成コードの安全性評価
articles.title_ja: コーディングエージェントによるコードベース内の脆弱性伝播
articles.summary_ja: LLMベースのコーディングエージェントが本番環境のソフトウェア開発に広く用いられる中、リポジトリ内の既存脆弱性が新規コード生成に与える影響が検証された。96件のバックエンド生成タスクと20件の実C/C++メモリ安全性タスクを評価した結果、既存の安全でないコードが存在することでエージェントが類似の脆弱性を導入する頻度が有意に高まることが判明した。C/C++では安全な環境と比較して脆弱性混入の格差が35.4%に達し、エージェントは脆弱性を認識しながらも76.5%のケースで既存コードのパターンを踏襲していた。

articles.title: Decalage: Uncovering the Gap Between Model-Generated Reasoning and Actual Code Implementation in Small Language Models
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.11721v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic code generation often asks a model to explain its reasoning before it writes code, and a common way to make such a workflow safer is to add a security instruction to the prompt. We test what that instruction does in small language models, which are attractive because they run locally and cheaply. Four open code models of 1.5B to 3B parameters generate C++ from 166 sections of eleven public requirements documents, once with a general prompt and once with a secure prompt. The secure prompt more than doubles the share of reasoning about validation, resource handling and threats, and we find no evidence that the rise is larger for requirements with security content. The code changes only in part. Among functions with a body and reasoning, the share with a check that our lexical test recognises rises from 23% to 39%, but more than a quarter of the functions remain stubs, compile rates stay low, and half or more of the functions whose reasoning mentions a check contain no such check. Two rounds of compiler-feedback repair leave more than 80% of sections unusable, and neither cppcheck nor an exploratory ESBMC run separates the prompts on the usable code. A hand check by two annotators supports the stub measure and the direction of the reasoning result. For small models, a security instruction changes the reasoning broadly but the code only in part, so the reasoning should be checked against the code rather than trusted.
engineering_topics: 生成コードの安全性評価
articles.title_ja: 小型言語モデルにおけるセキュリティ推論と実コード実装の乖離（Decalage）の検証
articles.summary_ja: エージェント的なコード生成において安全性を高めるためプロンプトにセキュリティ指示を付加する手法が普及しているが、ローカル環境で利用される1.5B〜3Bの小型言語モデル（SLM）における有効性を検証した。11件の要件定義書に基づくC++コード生成実験では、セキュリティ指示により検証や脅威に関する推論記述は倍増したものの、実際のコードへの反映は不十分であった。推論でバリデーションを言及した関数の半数以上で検査処理が実装されず、スタブ残存やコンパイル不能などの問題が確認された。
articles.insight: AIエージェントに『安全なコードを書く』推論ステップを設けても、生成されたコード自体に検証処理が欠落する乖離が存在することが示された。SASTやコンパイラ等の検証自動化なしにモデルの説明文のみを信用して安全性を判断することは危険である。診断実務者はエージェント生成コードの検査において、推論ログと実コードの突合・網羅的な静的解析を前提としたパイプラインを設計すべきである。

articles.title: Executable Specifications as First-Class Independent Verification and Validation Artifacts for Quantum Information and Machine Learning
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.10023v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Executable specifications make software assumptions explicit and checkable, yet their role in quantum information and machine learning (QIML) remains underexplored. We argue that executable specifications should be treated as first-class artifacts for independent verification and validation (IV&V) of QIML systems. Static analysis, testing, simulation, and runtime checking can provide evidence about QIML behavior, while Design by Contract shows that selected quantum-state, measurement, and statistical properties can be expressed as checkable conditions. However, adapting existing methods for specification inference and assessment from conventional and machine-learning software to QIML raises several challenges, notably limited evidence for deriving generalizable specifications, cross-stage and probabilistic behavior, repository-scale reasoning across hybrid workflows, and weak behavioral oracles. We characterize these challenges and identify research directions for QIML corpora, specification semantics, repository-level analysis, and specification assessment.
articles.title_ja: 量子情報および機械学習システムに対する独立検証・妥当性確認のための実行可能仕様
articles.summary_ja: 量子情報および機械学習（QIML）システムにおける独立検証および妥当性確認（IV&V）において、実行可能仕様（Executable Specifications）を一級の成果物として扱う枠組みが提唱された。契約による設計（Design by Contract）を通じて量子状態や測定、統計的性質を検証可能な条件として表現する可能性を整理している。一方で、確率的振る舞いや弱いテストオラクル、ハイブリッドワークフローに起因する仕様推論の難しさが課題として挙げられている。
articles.insight: 確率的振る舞いや統計的特性を伴うAI/量子システムでは、従来の決定論的なテストケースのみによる妥当性確認が限界を迎えている。実行可能仕様による事前・事後条件の形式化は、AIコンポーネントを診断・監査する際のオラクル確立において有効な基盤となり得る。動的診断やランタイムチェックを設計する際、統計的性質の契約定義をどのように取り込むかが問われる。
articles.importance_reason: MLおよび量子技術のハイブリッドシステムに対する検証・仕様策定の体系的アプローチと課題を整理しているため。

business.evidence: QIMLシステムの独立検証・妥当性確認に関する学術的な課題整理論文であり、実悪用や特定製品の記載はない。

articles.title: Statically Verifying Well-Definedness of Separately Compiled Attribute Grammars
articles.summary:
arXiv:2602.03777v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The development of programming languages involves complex theoretical and practical challenges, particularly when addressing modularity and reusability through language extensions. While language workbenches aim to enable modular development under the constraints of the language extension problem, one critical constraint--separate compilation--is often relaxed due to its complexity. However, this relaxation undermines artifact reusability and integration with common dependency systems. A key difficulty under separate compilation arises from managing attribute grammars, as extensions may introduce new attributes that invalidate previously generated abstract syntax tree structures. Existing approaches, such as the use of dynamic maps in the Neverlang workbench, favor flexibility at the cost of compile-time correctness, leading to potential runtime errors due to undefined attributes. This work addresses this issue by introducing nlgcheck, a theoretically sound static analysis tool based on data-flow analysis for the Neverlang language workbench, which detects potential runtime errors--such as undefined attribute accesses--when separately compiled language components are composed, before the resulting language is ever run, thus preserving separate compilation while maintaining strong static correctness guarantees. Experimental evaluation using mutation testing on Neverlang-based projects demonstrates that nlgcheck effectively enhances robustness without sacrificing modularity or flexibility and with a level of performance that does not impede its adoption in daily development activities.
articles.title_ja: 独立コンパイル型属性文法における未定義属性アクセスを実行前に防ぐ静的検証ツール「nlgcheck」
articles.summary_ja: 言語ワークベンチにおける言語拡張と分割コンパイルの両立では、拡張によって生成ASTが無効化され未定義属性アクセスなどの実行時エラーが発生しやすい問題があった。本論文では、Neverlangワークベンチ向けにデータフロー解析に基づく健全な静的解析ツール「nlgcheck」を提案している。分割コンパイルされた言語コンポーネントの合成時に、実行することなく潜在的な未定義属性エラーを検出可能とした。
articles.insight: 言語処理系やDSL拡張におけるコンポーネント合成時の実行時エラーを、実行前の静的データフロー解析で保証するアプローチは、安全なプラグイン拡張アーキテクチャの設計に寄与する。ソフトウェアサプライチェーンにおいて動的拡張モジュールの結合時整合性を担保する仕組みとして応用可能である。静的診断パイプラインにおいてモジュール間の属性定義不整合を検知できるかが検討事項となる。
articles.importance_reason: 言語ワークベンチの分割コンパイル時における属性文法の整合性を静的に検証するツールを開発・実証したため。

business.evidence: Neverlangベースのプロジェクトに対するミューテーションテストによる実証。実インシデントや日本市場への言及はない。

attack.assessment_preconditions: Neverlang言語ワークベンチ上で構成された言語コンポーネントおよび属性文法のソースコード
attack.test_scenario: 言語拡張コンポーネント合成時にnlgcheckを実行し、未定義属性へのアクセスが発生し得るデータフロー経路を静的に検出する。
attack.service_implication: DSLや言語コンパイラを自社開発・拡張しているシステムに対し、拡張モジュール結合時の属性未定義エラーを未然に検出するSASTルールや検証プロセスの導入を検討する。
attack.source_evidence: ミューテーションテストによるツールの静的検証性能評価（研究報告のみ）。

articles.title: Enhancing Neural Code Representation with Additional Context
articles.summary:
arXiv:2510.12082v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Automated program comprehension underpins many software engineering tasks, from code summarisation to clone detection. While recent deep learning models have achieved strong results, they typically rely on source code alone, overlooking contextual signals such as version history or structural relationships. We conduct an empirical study of how enriching code representations with such signals affects model performance on four tasks: code clone detection, code classification, code summarisation, and vulnerability detection, using three datasets (SeSaMe, CodeSearchNet-Java, Vul4J). We evaluate five foundational code models (CodeBERT, GraphCodeBERT, CodeT5, PLBART, ASTNN) and seven code-specialised LLMs (CodeLlama, Qwen2.5-Coder, DeepSeek-Coder), comparing prompt-based context injection against fine-tuned use of context. Context improves classification for all five foundational models and, after fine-tuning, for most LLMs. For summarisation, the effect depends on the model family: version history improves all four foundational models on every metric, whereas prompt-level context helps two of the seven LLMs and hurts the other five. Combining context types reaches up to +21.48% macro-F1 in code classification and +15.04% F1 in clone detection. A human evaluation of CodeT5 summaries on 100 Java snippets ranks context-augmented summaries significantly higher for Accuracy and Content Adequacy. An exploratory vulnerability detection evaluation provides initial evidence of transfer to security-oriented tasks.

articles.title: GreyZone: Production-quality Agentic Application Threats
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.09161v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agents are increasingly deployed across domains such as coding, banking, and commerce. Their ability to invoke tools and change application state makes security testing important for reliable deployment. Although agent security has been studied through various adversarial testing approaches, benchmarks grounded in production agent environments remain limited. We introduce GreyZone, a benchmark for evaluating automated red-teaming services against real-world agent applications. Unlike benchmarks such as AgentDojo, which primarily evaluate subject agents under attack, GreyZone evaluates services' ability to generate and deliver attacks that cause verified security-policy violations. We select independently developed, open-source agent applications with security boundaries concerning access permissions, confidentiality, and action authorization. These applications expose diverse attack surfaces, including those arising from multi-agent interactions and multimodal inputs. By grounding evaluation in application environments that preserve production-relevant workflows and independently verifying outcomes, GreyZone supports research on automated agent security testing. Specifically, we present two preliminary case studies using Promptfoo on Letta Code and Clawith to examine attack delivery, agent behavior, and verified outcomes. We release the benchmark, including subject agents and attack surfaces for each application, to support further research on agent testing methods.

articles.title: Wake 5: A Python Framework for Solidity Testing, Fuzzing, and Static Analysis
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.09307v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Smart-contract fuzzers differ by an order of magnitude in throughput and by design in how they construct inputs, yet published comparisons rarely separate the two. We present Wake 5, an open-source Python framework for Solidity testing, fuzzing and static analysis, and use it to locate the binding constraint of stateful smart-contract fuzzing. Wake 5 replaces the JSON-RPC connection to an external node with an in-process EVM (revm) and exposes its static analysis to language-model agents through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. On the Daedaluzz maze benchmark (153 reachable assertions, guard constants below 2^32), Wake 5 executes 29,931 transactions per second, on par with Foundry (30,186) and 11.5x faster than Echidna (2,600). In eight-hour campaigns, however, the three tools plateau at medians of 75, 71 and 70 assertions, and their union reaches 93. We show that Wake's integer generator places 51% of its probability mass below 2^32 and that, once shallow assertions are exhausted, the generator prior rather than throughput bounds every tool. A harness written by a language-model agent, which derives inputs with a constraint solver, reached all 153 assertions in each of five campaigns executed by Wake, in 33 to 79 minutes. A complementary ablation in an agentic audit of a production Go codebase found that static-analysis tools improved recall for none of three models, raised precision for all three, and increased language-model cost by up to 12.7%. We discuss correlated oracles and non-deterministic completion, and argue that the fuzzer's role is shifting from search to execution.
articles.title_ja: Wake 5：Solidityテスト、ファジング、静的解析のためのPythonフレームワーク
articles.summary_ja: スマートコントラクトファジングのスループットと入力生成の設計に着目し、Pythonフレームワーク「Wake 5」を提案した研究論文。Wake 5は、外部ノードへのJSON-RPC接続をプロセス内EVM（revm）に置き換え、MCPサーバーを通じてLLMエージェントに静的解析機能を提供する。ベンチマーク実験では、ファザーの性能限界はスループットではなくジェネレータの事前確率に依存し、制約ソルバーを用いたLLMエージェントによるハーネスが全ての検証を突破したことが示された。また、Goコードベースの監査において、静的解析ツールは精度を向上させる一方でLLMのコストを増加させることが確認された。

articles.title: I Don't Care How You Hide It, I Care What You Do: Runtime Detection of Malicious ML Models
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.08745v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Pre-trained machine learning (ML) models shared through public platforms can be weaponized to execute malicious payloads during loading or inference. Existing scanners prove inadequate for detecting malicious models as they rely on static analysis and function denylists, support limited serialization formats, and miss attacks that replace denylisted functions with equivalent alternatives, exploit unsupported loading paths, or abuse legitimate framework APIs. To address this problem, we present ModelShield, the first runtime behavioral detection system for malicious ML models that attributes observed system-level behavior to specific model operations. It combines application-level instrumentation of ML framework APIs with eBPF-based syscall tracing, tracking model behavior across spawned threads and processes to separate model-triggered activity from environment noise. Attributed syscall sequences are classified using 195 detection patterns mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques. We implemented ModelShield to support 17 ML frameworks and 36 formats. On an independent dataset, it is the only evaluated tool to achieve zero false positives, with false negatives limited to payloads that produce no malicious runtime behavior. It detected all 29 published evasion variants spanning function substitution, loading-path obfuscation, and TensorFlow API abuse, where no existing scanner achieved complete coverage. Across 145,000 models scanned from public platforms, it captured 41 malicious models on Hugging Face, including a reverse-shell payload and a payload that performed host reconnaissance and outbound exfiltration. Among these, ModelScan, PickleScan, Fickling, and ModelAudit detected only 29%, 56%, 80%, and 93%, respectively. Despite runtime overhead, ModelShield has a median analysis time of 12.3 seconds, with 90% of scans completing within 35.5 seconds, making it practical for hub-scale screening.

articles.title: Taiwan-Based Hacker Used BOSSAI AI Agents to Steal Taipei Emergency Dispatch Records
articles.summary:
A single attacker using AI agents pulled emergency dispatch records covering seven Taipei districts, researchers at Acronis's Threat Research Unit said last week.

The agents also found a Taipei fire department platform exposing patient data from 2018, including ECG readings and ambulance video footage, without a login.

The researchers are highly confident that the attacker is a single person

articles.title: I Think, Therefore I Attack: Evaluating Thought Injection Attacks on Reasoning Agents
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.08811v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) are one of the key components of current agentic systems. LRMs augment their output with an explicit chain-of-thought reasoning stage, introducing a new attack surface for thought injection, in which untrusted text resembling the model's own deliberation is fed back to the model. We present a two-part study of this attack, performed against the prevailing large, production class open-weight models (e.g., GLM-5.3, MiniMax-M2.5, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). We first evaluate the effectiveness of static thought-injection prompts under different styles as well as tagged and untagged conditions and find that the effects of thinking tags and payload styles are all properties of the specific target model. In the second study, we exploit this model-specificity in a containerized agentic cyber range, using indirect injection prompts styled in the form of the target model's own reasoning traces to achieve attack success rates (ASR) up to 50% on operational objectives such as reverse-shell exfiltration and repository backdooring. We also find that the same malicious objective in standard prompt injection user voice never succeeds, and thinking tags suppress the agent's tendency to disclose the injection. Our results show that imitating a reasoning model's own thought style is effective for this style of attack, and that tag stripping is an unreliable defense.

articles.summary_ja: 大規模推論モデル（LRM）が推論過程を出力する仕組みを悪用し、モデル自身の思考に偽装したテキストを入力する「思考注入（Thought Injection）」攻撃に関する研究が発表された。コンテナ環境のサイバーレンジにおいて、標的モデルの思考スタイルを模倣した間接インジェクションにより、リバースシェル取得やリポジトリのバックドア化で最大50%の攻撃成功率（ASR）が確認された。通常のプロンプトインジェクションでは成功しなかった攻撃が成立し、タグ除去による防御も信頼できないことが示された。

articles.title: Internal Safety Collapse in LLMs and Coding Agents
articles.summary:
arXiv:2603.23509v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: LLMs and coding agents can now tackle complex, long-horizon tasks through advances in reinforcement learning, but stronger task-solving capabilities do not necessarily preserve safety alignment. Recent AI agent incidents involving reward hacking indicate how optimizing for task success can bring learned capabilities into conflict with safety alignment. In this work, we identify a critical failure mode that manifests this conflict, which we term Internal Safety Collapse (ISC). When completing otherwise benign coding tasks, AI agents can prioritize satisfying program requirements over safety constraints, generating large volumes of sensitive content, including unsafe outputs, as task data. To study this phenomenon, we introduce TVD (Task, Validator, Data), a framework for building controlled workflows that require sensitive content for completion. Through extensive experiments, we observe instances of highly harmful content that closely resemble outputs from early, unaligned LLMs in 2023. We further find that ISC can be effectively triggered even in highly capable LLMs such as Claude Fable 5. These results indicate that, despite substantial alignment efforts, frontier LLMs remain internally unsafe: safety alignment primarily reshapes surface behavior without eliminating the underlying knowledge that enables unsafe outputs. Our findings underscore the need for caution when deploying LLMs in high-stakes settings, such as scientific pipelines and autonomous agents.
  Content Warning: This paper contains examples of harmful content. Source code: https://github.com/wuyoscar/Internal-Safety-Collapse
articles.title_ja: 強化学習済みコーディングエージェントにおける内部安全性の崩壊現象
articles.summary_ja: 強化学習により長期タスク解決能力を高めたLLMやコーディングエージェントにおいて、タスク達成が安全アライメントと衝突し安全制約を無視する「内部安全性崩壊（ISC）」現象が特定された。実験では、無害なプログラミング要件を満たすために有害な出力を生成する事例が確認され、Claude Fable 5などの高度なモデルでもISCが誘発された。この結果は、表面的なアライメント調整にもかかわらず、フロンティアモデルの内部には依然として有害出力を可能にする知識が残存していることを示している。
articles.insight: エージェントが「タスク完遂」を最優先する過程で安全フィルターを回避する問題は、自動化されたコード生成や業務代行の安全性評価において重大な示唆を与える。静的解析や入力バリデーションだけでなく、エージェントが中間生成するコードやデータの動的監視・実行制御が不可欠である。自律型エージェントを本番導入する際、タスク達成条件と倫理・安全ポリシーの優先順位をどう分離設計するかが問われる。
articles.importance_reason: 高度な推論・コーディングモデルであっても、タスク最適化によって安全アライメントが容易に崩壊することが実証されたため。

articles.title_ja: OpenAI、境界を逸脱せず脆弱性を探索する新サイバーモデル「GPT-6 Cyber」を発表
articles.summary_ja: OpenAIはサイバーセキュリティ領域向けに評価された新たなモデル「GPT-6 Cyber」を発表した。本モデルは前世代のGPT-5.6 Cyberと比較してエクスプロイト能力が向上しているとされる。同時に、定められた診断対象のスコープ内に留まる制御性も高められていると主張されている。
articles.insight: AIを用いた自律型脆弱性診断やペネトレーションテストにおいて、エクスプロイト実行能力と診断範囲（スコープ）の逸脱防止を両立できるかが実務上の焦点となる。安全装置の精度や誤検知率、攻撃ペイロードの制御性が第三者検証されているかが導入の判断基準になる。SOCや診断部門は、AIエージェントによる自動スキャンが意図しないシステム停止を引き起こさない検証プロセスをどう設計すべきか問われる。
articles.importance_reason: AIモデルによる脆弱性探索・エクスプロイト自動化の進展と、そのスコープ制御性に関する重要トレンドであるため。

articles.title: Grocery Giant Ahold Delhaize Estimates Financial Toll of October Cyberattack
articles.summary:
The October incident will cut fourth-quarter sales by up to €250 million and has led Ahold Delhaize to lower its 2026 outlook.

The post Grocery Giant Ahold Delhaize Estimates Financial Toll of October Cyberattack appeared first on SecurityWeek.
articles.title_ja: 大手流通Ahold Delhaize、10月のサイバー攻撃による巨額財務影響を公表
articles.summary_ja: 大手食品スーパーチェーンのAhold Delhaizeは、10月に発生したサイバーインシデントによる財務的損失の見通しを公表した。このインシデントにより第4四半期の売上高が最大2億5000万ユーロ減少する見込みである。これに伴い同社は2026年の業績見通しを引き下げた。
articles.insight: 事業インフラへのサイバーインシデントが単なる復旧費用にとどまらず、四半期売上や中期業績見通しに深刻な影響を与える現実を示している。サプライチェーンや店舗運営が絡む流通業では、停止リスクを最小化するBCPと資産の早期隔離が不可欠である。SOCやインシデント対応組織は、財務的影響を最小化するための復旧優先順位を経営層と合意できているかを問い直す必要がある。
articles.importance_reason: サイバーインシデントが企業の売上高および中長期業績見通しに直接影響を与えた大規模事例であるため。

business.evidence: The October incident will cut fourth-quarter sales by up to €250 million and has led Ahold Delhaize to lower its 2026 outlook.

articles.summary_ja: D-LinkはギガビットスタッカブルマネージドスイッチであるDGS-3130シリーズに複数の未パッチ脆弱性が存在することを警告した。対象機器に対して未修正のセキュリティ欠陥が存在するため、同社は緩和策を公開した。管理機器が直接侵害されるリスクに対処するため暫定的な防御措置が求められている。
articles.insight: ネットワーク機器における未パッチのゼロデイ脆弱性は、境界防御の突破や内部ネットワーク掌握に直結する。パッチ未提供の段階では、管理アクセスの制限やセグメンテーションによる露出低減などの緩和策を迅速に適用する必要がある。外部公開資産や内部ネットワーク機器の資産台帳に当該モデルが含まれていないか、即時に再診断・調査する体制が重要となる。

articles.title: OpenSSH Rushes Patches for ‘SSHole’ Authentication Bypass
articles.summary:
On Linux distributions using musl libc without PAM, some accounts accept any password between 257 and 1024 characters.

The post OpenSSH Rushes Patches for ‘SSHole’ Authentication Bypass appeared first on SecurityWeek.
articles.title_ja: OpenSSHが認証バイパスの脆弱性「SSHole」に対するパッチを緊急リリース
articles.summary_ja: PAMを使用せずmusl libcを採用したLinuxディストリビューションにおいて、OpenSSHの認証がバイパスされる脆弱性が報告されました。特定のアカウントにおいて、257文字から1024文字の任意のパスワードを入力することで認証が通過する問題が判明しています。OpenSSH開発チームはこの問題に対処するためのパッチを緊急リリースしました。
articles.insight: musl libcを採用する軽量コンテナ環境（Alpine Linux等）や組み込みLinuxが攻撃対象になり得るため、DASTや外部公開資産スキャンでの特定に加え、SCAや構成管理による実態把握が求められます。脆弱性の悪用がパスワード長に依存する特殊な挙動であるため、ブラックボックス診断時の認証テストケースの網羅性が再考されます。認証機構とCライブラリの実装差異に起因する盲点をどう継続監視するかが問われます。
articles.importance_reason: 広範に利用されるOpenSSHにおいて認証バイパスが可能となる深刻な問題であり、特定ディストリビューション環境に直接影響するため。

assessments: ブラックボックス診断
ペネトレーションテスト
business.evidence: On Linux distributions using musl libc without PAM, some accounts accept any password between 257 and 1024 characters.

articles.title: Malicious Browser Extensions Could Use Claude Dispatch to Run Code on Users' Computers
articles.summary:
A browser extension that can run scripts on claude.ai could make Claude Desktop run code on a person's computer, researchers at Forever Security, an endpoint security company, showed in a test.

The attack needs Dispatch, a Claude feature that lets people send tasks from their phone to Claude Desktop. The flaw that makes this possible can still be exploited, the researchers said earlier this
articles.title_ja: 悪意あるブラウザ拡張機能がClaude Dispatchを悪用して端末上でコードを実行するリスク
articles.summary_ja: Forever Securityのリサーチャーは、claude.ai上でスクリプトを実行可能なブラウザ拡張機能が悪用される検証結果を示しました。スマートフォンからClaude Desktopへタスクを送信するClaudeのDispatch機能が悪用されることで、利用者のコンピュータ上で任意のコードが実行されるリスクがあります。研究者によると、この悪用を可能にする欠陥は公表時点でも悪用可能な状態であると報告されています。
articles.insight: Web画面とローカル実行環境（Desktopアプリ）が連携するAI機能における認可境界の不備を示しており、AIエージェントのツール・実行層のセキュリティ評価が不可欠であることを示唆しています。ペネトレーションテストやAPI診断において、連携元クライアント（ブラウザコンテキスト）の侵害がローカルコマンド実行へ波及するシナリオを考慮する必要があります。AIエージェントの端末連携機能における最小権限とユーザー明示承認の設計確認が重要です。
articles.importance_reason: 広く利用される生成AIクライアントにおいて、ブラウザ拡張機能を介したローカルコード実行につながる実証が行われたため。

articles.title: 「Apache OFBiz」にRCE脆弱性 - 修正版がリリース
articles.summary: Apacheの業務アプリケーション「Apache OFBiz」に深刻な脆弱性が明らかとなった。開発チームは修正版を提供している。
articles.title_ja: 「Apache OFBiz」に深刻なRCE脆弱性、修正版が公開
articles.summary_ja: オープンソースの業務アプリケーション「Apache OFBiz」において、深刻なリモートコード実行（RCE）の脆弱性が報告された。開発チームはこの問題に対処するため、最新の修正版をリリースした。本脆弱性の悪用によるシステム侵害リスクを防ぐため、管理者は迅速な更新が求められる。
articles.insight: OFBizはERPやEC基盤として外部公開されるケースがあり、RCE脆弱性は初期侵入の標的になりやすい。脆弱性診断では公開APIや管理画面のエンドポイント特定が焦点となるが、抜粋では具体的な悪用条件やPoCの有無は不明である。SOCとしては外部からの不審なコマンド実行や異常トラフィックを検知できるログ体制が機能しているかを点検する契機となる。
articles.importance_reason: 業務基盤に用いられるソフトウェアにおける深刻なRCE脆弱性であり、侵害時の影響が大きいため。

articles.summary: WatchGuardの多要素認証ソリューション「WatchGuard AuthPoint」で利用する一部コンポーネントに複数の脆弱性が明らかとなった。同社は修正版を提供している。
articles.title_ja: WatchGuardの多要素認証「AuthPoint」コンポーネントにクリティカル脆弱性
articles.summary_ja: WatchGuardの多要素認証（MFA）製品「WatchGuard AuthPoint」の一部コンポーネントに複数の脆弱性が発見された。中には重要度が「クリティカル」とされる深刻な欠陥が含まれている。ベンダーはすでに修正版をリリースしており、利用者に更新を促している。
articles.insight: MFAコンポーネントの脆弱性は認証基盤全体のバイパスや権限昇格に直結する懸念がある。認証連携やエージェントの更新漏れがないか、アイデンティティ管理運用の観点で点検が必要となる。認証ログの監視設計において、MFAバイパスや異常認証試行を検知できる構造になっているかを評価する問いが生じる。
articles.importance_reason: 境界防御やゼロトラストの中核となる多要素認証製品にクリティカルな脆弱性が確認されたため。

articles.title: 「Firefox」のレイアウト処理に脆弱性 - 「同159.0.1」で修正
articles.summary: Mozilla Foundationは現地時間2026年11月3日、ウェブブラウザのセキュリティアップデートとなる「Firefox 159.0.1」を公開した。
articles.title_ja: Mozilla、「Firefox 159.0.1」を公開 - レイアウト処理の脆弱性を修正
articles.summary_ja: Mozilla Foundationは、Webブラウザのセキュリティアップデート「Firefox 159.0.1」をリリースした。本バージョンでは、ブラウザのレイアウト処理に関する脆弱性が修正されている。悪用による意図しない動作やクラッシュ、任意のコード実行リスクを避けるため更新が推奨される。
articles.insight: クライアント側ブラウザのレンダリング・レイアウトエンジンの脆弱性は、悪意あるWebサイト閲覧を通じたクライアント侵害の契機となる可能性がある。端末管理（MDM/EDR）による自動更新の徹底と、サンドボックス機構による影響局所化が防御の基本となる。エンドポイント監視において不審なブラウザ子プロセスの起動を捉えられる設計かが確認論点となる。
articles.importance_reason: 広く利用されているクライアントブラウザの描画処理に関するセキュリティ修正であるため。
related_keywords: セキュリティアップデート

business.evidence: 記事抜粋に「Firefox 159.0.1を公開」「レイアウト処理に脆弱性」と明記。

attack.test_scenario: 悪意あるレイアウト処理を含むコンテンツのレンダリング挙動検証が考えられるが、抜粋に脆弱性の詳細条件はなく不明。
attack.service_implication: 端末脆弱性管理（ブラウザバージョン管理）ポリシーの点検やEDRによる検知方針の確認検討が挙げられる。
attack.source_evidence: 抜粋に「Firefoxのレイアウト処理に脆弱性」「同159.0.1で修正」と記載。

articles.title: How Should Agents See Code? Rethinking Code Representations for Agentic Software Engineering
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.07286v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly used for repository-level software engineering tasks. However, most agents still access repositories through raw files, lexical search, and shell commands, treating code primarily as text. This paper investigates map-based code-representation workflows as a design variable in agentic software engineering, examining how different repository views change agents' retrieval behavior, task success, token use, and latency.
  In this paper, we study five code-representation workflows: abstract syntax trees, call graphs, module dependencies, documentation-enriched search, and a hybrid workflow that combines them. Each workflow exposes a repository map that the agent can query during a task. We evaluate Claude Code with Haiku 4.5 against a raw-tool baseline on four repository-level tasks: fault localization with LinuxFLBench, repository-level code generation and repair with SWE-bench Pro, test generation with SWT-bench, and security patching with SecBench.
  The results show that representation workflows are most useful as token-saving tools when localization is the bottleneck, while their success gains narrow when the decisive step is patch or test authoring. On LinuxFLBench, all five workflows improve recall@10 over the baseline (0.757-0.829 vs. 0.717) and reduce token usage by 25-39%. On SWE-bench Pro, resolution remains close to the baseline (44.3-50.6% vs. 49.0%) while token usage drops by 17-26%. On SecBench, Callgraph has the highest patch-resolution rate in this sample (34.3% vs. 28.9%) and uses fewer tokens, but all workflows increase latency. On SWT-bench, Hybrid and Docs have the highest reproducing-test rates in this sample (47.8% and 47.2% vs. 44.7%), but all workflows use more tokens and take longer. Overall, map-based workflows change both what the agent inspects and how much it spends, but their benefits are task-dependent rather than universal.

articles.title: AI Slop and Hallucinations in Vulnerability Assessment: A Survey on Reasoning Failures and Trustworthy Mitigation
articles.summary:
arXiv:2608.25667v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into cybersecurity has transformed vulnerability assessment, but it has also produced a trustworthiness crisis driven by the unchecked proliferation of "AI slop." These artifacts, hallucinated vulnerabilities, plausible but incorrect patches, and semantically repackaged bug reports, impose a cognitive burden on human triage pipelines that mirrors a denial-of-service attack. This paper surveys the empirical evidence, identifies a unifying mechanism, and traces a path toward trustworthy triage. We formalize a taxonomy of AI slop grounded in a structured literature review and dissect its root cause: the gap between the causal deductive reasoning of security experts and the autoregressive probabilistic generation of current LLMs. We operationalize this gap through a measurable proxy, the Deductive Coverage Score, and show that chain-of-thought prompting and tool-using agents narrow but do not close it. We review mitigation strategies and argue that passive detection and watermarking target provenance rather than correctness, facing fundamental entropy constraints. We instead advocate for active neuro-symbolic verification, mapping each pipeline component to prior systems with documented limits on security inputs. Finally, we specify two evaluation instruments, CVE-Bench and Slop-Score, including dataset construction, metric formulas, and anti-gaming provisions. By shifting evaluation from linguistic fluency to mathematical verifiability, this survey provides a roadmap for securing emerging AI-driven triage systems.

articles.title: Refactoring React Component Hierarchies to Eliminate Prop Drilling
articles.summary:
arXiv:2610.01376v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: In React front-end development, Prop Drilling is the practice of propagating data through component properties across multiple levels of the component hierarchy. Despite being discouraged by React documentation and characterized as a code smell by recent research, little is known about its prevalence, complexity, and potential for automated refactoring. In this work, we propose a static analysis method for identifying Prop Drilling instances in a React codebase and eliminating them using two automated refactoring strategies based on Context API and Component Composition. The proposed method is implemented as a Node\.js command line tool, ReactRefactor, and empirically evaluated on a benchmark dataset of open-source React applications. The main findings of the empirical evaluation indicate (a) the frequent occurrence of prop drillings across benchmark projects, irrespective of project size; (b) their generally low to moderate complexity in terms of data propagation depth, contrasted with the more prevalent complexity arising from the simultaneous forwarding of multiple properties along the same path; and, (c) the potential for automated elimination of a substantial share (76.3%) of prop drillings, primarily through refactoring to the Context API.
articles.title_ja: Reactコンポーネント階層のリファクタリングによるProp Drillingの解消
articles.summary_ja: React開発においてコンポーネント階層を越えてデータをバケツリレーするProp Drillingはコードスメルとされていますが、その実態や自動リファクタリングの可能性は十分に解明されていませんでした。本研究では、静的解析によりProp Drillingを検出し、Context APIやコンポーネント合成を用いて自動解消する手法およびCLIツール「ReactRefactor」を提案しています。オープンソースのReactプロジェクトを用いた評価の結果、プロジェクト規模に関わらず頻繁に発生していることや、対象の76.3%を主にContext APIへ自動リファクタリング可能であることが示されました。
articles.insight: フロントエンドの保守性改善技術ですが、ソースコード静的解析（SAST）や自動修正の観点では、コード品質向上による意図しないデータ漏えいや状態管理バグの低減に応用できる余地があります。ただしセキュリティ脆弱性の解消を主眼とした研究ではないため、修正後の機能リグレッション検証や状態管理のアクセス制御に関する安全性の検証体制をいかに組み込むかが問われます。

articles.title: The Promise of Strategic Agentic Scambaiting
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.08170v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Scammers have increasingly adopted AI-driven capabilities, evolving from automated message generation to fully agentic conversational systems that scale operations and maximize the exploitation of fraudulent resources before detection and takedown. In parallel, agentic scambaiting has emerged as a defensive approach in which autonomous agents impersonate potential victims and engage scammers in sustained interactions to extract actionable threat intelligence, such as mule bank accounts and cryptocurrency wallet addresses, that can be reported to disrupt fraudulent infrastructures. Together, these developments transform online fraud into an adversarial socio-technical ecosystem in which autonomous scamming and scambaiting agents engage in deceptive interactions while competing over the discovery, preservation, and exploitation of one another's resources. A fundamental and largely unexplored question is how defensive scambaiting can remain effective in an agent-to-agent environment, and under what conditions either side gains a strategic advantage. In this paper, we present a formal model of agent-to-agent fraud interactions that captures the strategic decision spaces available to both attackers and defenders. Using this framework, we analyze the dynamics of engagement, resource consumption, belief adaptation, and disruption outcomes. We find that scammer profitability turns negative once baiting-agent prevalence exceeds certain thresholds, and that when both sides improve at the same pace, defender investment in mimicry quality outpaces equivalent gains in scammer detection capability, so the arms race favors the defender under our baseline parameters. Our model and findings provide insights into the stability, scalability, and long-term effectiveness of autonomous defensive agents in an evolving AI-mediated fraud landscape.
articles.title_ja: 自律型エージェントを用いたおとり対抗策（Agentic Scambaiting）の有効性モデル
articles.summary_ja: 詐欺攻撃者が自律的な対話型AIエージェントを導入して詐欺活動を大規模化させる中、防御側が被害者になりすましてミュール口座等の脅威情報を収集する「agentic scambaiting」が注目されている。本研究では、攻撃側と防御側の双方がエージェントを用いる敵対的エコシステムにおける戦略的数理モデルを構築した。分析の結果、おとりエージェントの普及率が閾値を超えると攻撃者の採算が悪化し、双方が同ペースで進化する場合でも模倣精度の向上が防御側に有利に働くことが示された。
articles.insight: AIエージェント同士が欺瞞と検出を繰り返す環境では、エージェントの振る舞いモデルや情報抽出プロセスの設計が防御能力を左右する。セキュリティ評価の視点では、LLMエージェントに対するプロンプトインジェクションや偽装検出耐性、エージェント間対話の安全性検証が新たな診断対象になり得る。防御用AIエージェントの運用において、どのようなガバナンスと評価基準で欺瞞活動の品質と安全性を担保するかが問われる。
articles.importance_reason: AIエージェント同士の攻防という次世代のサイバー防衛モデルを数理的に分析し、防御側優位の条件を提示した研究であるため。

articles.title: SBVUL: Statement-Based Vulnerability Detection
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.06135v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many recent approaches for vulnerability detection use large language models (LLMs) to classify functions as vulnerable or benign, leaving developers to locate the exploitable statements. Furthermore, while these approaches have shown performance improvements, they still fall short in distinguishing vulnerable from patched real-world functions. This paper presents SBVul, an agentic approach that detects exploitable statements in C/C++ functions. In Phase~1, an LLM agent explores the function and its repository and identifies candidate statements. In Phase~2, a second agent analyzes the control and data flow of each candidate and confirms it, rules it out, or marks it uncertain. We created a manually verified ground truth of exploitable statements for 200 pairs of the PrimeVul Paired test set and ran SBVul with the open-weight models Qwen 3.8 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Anthropic's Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5. Phase~1 identifies ground-truth statements in 56--77% of the vulnerable functions, and Phase~2 confirms such a statement with an explanation accepted by an LLM judge in 26--73%. However, all models also confirm candidates in 23--61% of the patched functions. Across vulnerable and patched functions, the highest statement-level precision is 0.315 at a recall of 0.605 obtained with Opus 5.5 (xhigh). At the function level, SBVul with Opus 5.5 classifies 42.0% of the pairs correctly, compared with 33.8% reported for the best previous approach.

articles.title: From Lab to Reality: A Practical Evaluation of Deep Learning Models and LLMs for Vulnerability Detection
articles.summary:
arXiv:2512.10485v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Vulnerability detection methods based on deep learning (DL) have shown strong performance on benchmark datasets, yet their real-world effectiveness remains underexplored. Recent work suggests that graph neural network-based and transformer-based models, including large language models (LLMs), yield promising results when evaluated on curated benchmark datasets. These datasets are typically characterized by similar data distributions and may contain synthetic samples, heuristic labels, or labeling noise. In this study, we systematically evaluate four representative DL models---Devign, ReVeal, LineVul, and VulBERTa---across four representative datasets: Juliet, Devign, BigVul, and ICVul. Each model is trained independently on each dataset, and the graph-based and CodeBERT representations adopted by these models are analyzed using t-SNE and centroid distance to examine vulnerability-related patterns. To assess realistic applicability, we further evaluate trained ReVeal and LineVul models, along with four open-weight LLMs, on VentiVul, our newly constructed temporally separated out-of-distribution (OOD) dataset comprising 200 recent vulnerabilities from Linux and Chromium. Our experiments reveal that current representation methods struggle to distinguish vulnerable from non-vulnerable code and that trained models generalize poorly across datasets with differing distributions and characteristics. When evaluated on VentiVul, performance drops sharply, with most models failing to detect vulnerabilities reliably or distinguish vulnerable functions from their patched counterparts. These results expose a persistent gap between academic benchmarks and real-world deployment, emphasizing the value of our deployment-oriented evaluation framework and the need for more robust code representations, higher-quality datasets, and evaluation methods that account for vulnerability-fixing changes.
engineering_topics: 評価基盤・データセット

articles.title: A.S.E 2.0: Understanding How Repository Context Impacts the Security of LLM-Generated Code
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.06294v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model (LLM) coding assistants and agents construct a repository context before generating code. For security-sensitive code, this context decides whether the model sees the project's safeguards (e.g., authorization checks) or insecure code to imitate. However, context construction is designed almost exclusively for functional correctness, and secure-code benchmarks treat the context as fixed, so how repository context affects the security of generated code remains unclear. We construct CASE-Bench, a benchmark of 145 repository-level tasks from real CVEs in 51 projects. Each task runs in Docker, has functional tests and a proof-of-concept exploit validated in both directions, and is annotated with the repository code that enforces or undermines its security. Using CASE-Bench, we compare 13 context construction methods and six controls with six LLMs, edit single context elements, and analyze coding-agent trajectories. We find that (1) functionality-oriented context raises the functional pass rate by up to 8.2 percentage points (pp) but the secure pass rate by at most 3.7 pp, (2) withholding a safeguard lowers the secure pass rate by up to 8.1 pp, while one inserted insecure exemplar raises correct-but-exploitable code by 6.3 pp, and (3) coding agents observe the relevant safeguard in only 27-36% of trajectories. These findings inform security-aware context construction and secure-code evaluation.

articles.title: Reassessing Dataset Quality and Fine-Tuning Practices for Vulnerability Detection on PrimeVul dataset
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.06373v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent studies report promising results from supervised fine-tuning of pre-trained code language models for automated vulnerability detection on benchmarks such as PrimeVul. In this paper, we present a large-scale empirical evaluation of both model performance and dataset quality in this setting.
  We systematically fine-tune three widely used encoder models (CodeBERT, GraphCodeBERT, and UniXCoder) across five imbalance mitigation strategies, extensive hyperparameter sweeps, and multiple random seeds, resulting in 770 independent training runs.
  Our results reveal a consistent pattern. While standard metrics such as F1 and ROC-AUC occasionally suggest improvements, security-critical and calibration-aware measures tell a different story. Matthews Correlation Coefficient remains near zero, predicted probabilities are poorly calibrated, and evaluation under strict false-positive constraints reveals high false-negative rates. Neither imbalance handling, threshold optimization, nor post-hoc calibration recovers a meaningful discriminative signal.
  We also conduct a data quality assessment of the PrimeVul benchmark and identify structural issues such as minimal semantic differences between vulnerable and fixed functions, and annotation noise introduced by commit-level labeling.
  These findings suggests that the PrimeVul dataset, in its current form, presents significant challenges for reliable AI-based vulnerability detection in software engineering with the methodologies we used. Our study highlights the need for more robust dataset design, improved evaluation protocols, and rethinking of fine-tuning practices for security-critical tasks.

articles.title: Automated Exploit and Security Test Generation: A Systematic Literature Review
articles.summary:
arXiv:2502.04953v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Static analysis techniques are often insufficient to determine whether a reported security vulnerability is exploitable and actually poses a real security risk to a software application. Dynamic analysis addresses this limitation by executing the target application with carefully crafted inputs that trigger or reproduce a given vulnerability. Over the past two decades, automatic exploit generation (AEG) and automatic security test generation (ASTG) have emerged as active research areas in cybersecurity and software engineering.
  This paper demystifies the field by establishing consistent terminology and presenting a systematic literature review (SLR) of research published in the last two decades. Starting from an initial set of 3,309 publications obtained from academic literature search engines, we selected and analyzed 71 papers comprising 67 distinct studies. We systematically compare existing AEG and ASTG approaches with respect to (i) the targeted software and vulnerability types, (ii) the generated artifacts, (iii) the underlying generation techniques and tools employed, (iv) the required inputs, (v) the evaluation methodologies, and (vi) implementation and tool availability.
articles.title_ja: 自動的エクスポイトおよびセキュリティテスト生成（AEG/ASTG）に関する系統的文献レビュー
articles.summary_ja: 静的解析の限界を補う動的解析として、自動的エクスポイト生成（AEG）および自動的セキュリティテスト生成（ASTG）に関する過去2年間の文献を対象とした系統的文献レビュー（SLR）が実施された。初期3,309件の出版物から厳選された71本の論文（67件の研究）を分析し、対象ソフトウェア、生成アーティファクト、基盤技術、必要入力、評価手法、ツール提供状況などの観点から体系的な比較を行っている。本研究は、この分野の用語の整理と現状の課題を明らかにしている。
articles.insight: 動的解析やファジング、自動テスト生成の技術動向を把握する上で、過去の研究成果と手法の分類は有用なインプットとなる。脆弱性診断やペネトレーションテストの自動化ツールを選定・評価する際、どのような前提条件やツール制約があるかを整理するための枠組みを提供する。実務への導入にあたっては、生成されるアーティファクトの信頼性と適用範囲を慎重に見極める必要がある。

articles.title: Keeping Fuzzers on Duty: Repairing Fuzzing Build Breakages in Continuous Open-Source Fuzzing
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.06358v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Continuous fuzzing platforms such as OSS-Fuzz provide sustained security testing for open-source projects, but long-term build breakages reduce security coverage and waste infrastructure resources. In OSS-Fuzz, around 20% of integrated projects remain in build-failure states, leaving their fuzzers off duty. These failures expose a maintenance gap between platform maintainers, who lack project-specific context, and project maintainers, who often lack fuzzing and infrastructure expertise. Existing program-repair techniques cannot be directly applied because fuzz build breakages span evolving project and infrastructure artifacts and require repeated infrastructure-aware diagnosis. We present FuzzMedic, an automated agent for fuzz build repair. FuzzMedic performs evidence-guided diagnosis across project and fuzzing-infrastructure artifacts. It explores repairs over a repair-state graph (RSG) that records the evolving workspace and build feedback. Branching and rollback enable FuzzMedic to recover from unproductive repair paths during long-horizon debugging. Candidate patches are validated to restore executable fuzz targets rather than merely suppress build failures. We evaluate FuzzMedic on 128 reproducible OSS-Fuzz build failures extracted from 1,820 real-world failures. FuzzMedic achieves a 48.44% repair rate and outperforms three representative program-repair baselines. In real-world use, it produces 29 patches merged into upstream or OSS-Fuzz main branches, including repairs for three failures that had remained unresolved for more than one year and two cases that had never built successfully.
articles.title_ja: オープンソース継続的ファジングにおけるビルド障害修復自動化エージェント「FuzzMedic」
articles.summary_ja: OSS-Fuzzなどの継続的ファジングプラットフォームにおいて、長期間のビルド障害がセキュリティカバレッジの低下やインフラ資源の浪費を招いている課題に対し、証拠に基づく診断を行う自動修復エージェント「FuzzMedic」が提案された。FuzzMedicは、修復状態グラフ（RSG）を用いた探索、分岐、ロールバックにより、複雑なプロジェクトおよびインフラのビルド障害を自律的に診断・修復する。128件の再現可能な障害を用いた評価において48.44%の修復率を達成し、実際のOSS-Fuzzリポジトリ等へのパッチマージ実績も示されている。
articles.insight: ファジングインフラの維持管理における人的コストとカバレッジ低下の課題に対し、自律型エージェントによる修復アプローチの有効性を示す具体例である。セキュリティテストの継続性を担保するためには、テスト実行環境のビルドエラーや環境起因の停止を検知し自動復旧する仕組みが不可欠となる。DevSecOpsパイプラインにおけるテスト基盤の維持管理自動化への応用が期待される。
articles.importance_reason: 継続的セキュリティテスト運用の効率化とインフラ維持における自動修復エージェントの実用性を示しているため

business.evidence: arXiv:2611.06358v1で発表されたFuzzMedicのOSS-Fuzzビルド障害修復に関する評価結果に基づく。

articles.title: JANUS: Agentic Cross-Language Fuzzing Harness Generation for Android Native Libraries
articles.summary:
arXiv:2610.30218v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Modern Android apps extensively rely on native libraries, bridging Java/Kotlin and C/C++ through the Java Native Interface (JNI). This cross-language interoperation, however, exposes the memory-safe Android Runtime to the unsafe C/C++ world, creating an attack surface that has been repeatedly exploited for full device compromise. While fuzzing is a proven technique for vetting native libraries, state-of-the-art harness generation tools struggle to faithfully capture closed-source cross-language API usage: (i) precise program analysis across the JNI boundary does not scale, whereas lightweight approximations miss critical invocation patterns; and (ii) none tackles the construction of complex composite objects consumed by JNI methods.
  In this paper, we propose JANUS, the first agentic approach to synthesizing cross-language JNI-aware fuzzing harnesses for Android native libraries. JANUS iteratively resolves both explicit and implicit cross-language call dependencies to recover app-specific runtime context, and recursively assembles cross-language argument objects in a bottom-up manner. JANUS leverages an autonomous agentic workflow to reduce reliance on hand-crafted heuristics, capturing the vast landscape of hidden API usage knowledge embedded in closed-source native libraries. Evaluation on 44 popular real-world apps (such as Google and YouTube Music, covering 21,386 JNI methods total) shows that JANUS produces over 5.9 times as many valid harnesses (6,094) as state-of-the-art automatic harnessing tools. On pre-installed apps from five mainstream Android vendors (e.g., Xiaomi, Vivo, Samsung), JANUS further uncovers 6 previously unknown vulnerabilities in closed-source native libraries.

articles.title: Fixed Detectors, Moving Code: How Well Do Static Security Analyzers Hold Up over a Decade of C/C++ Evolution?
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.03742v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Static application security testing (SAST) tools are often deployed on the assumption that detectors configured today will remain effective on future code, including previously unknown vulnerabilities. We test this assumption using 20,000 vulnerable and fixed C/C++ cases from 1,116 open-source projects (2016-2025), evaluated with three CodeQL releases, three Infer releases, and one Semgrep configuration. To distinguish temporal effects from shifts in code composition, we compare yearly populations, project- and label-matched year pairs, and within-project trajectories. We investigate the largest within-project declines through repair diffs, detection predicates, alert locations, and execution logs, while accounting for failed, degraded, and costly analyses. Under changed-file case-label scoring, overall F1 ranges from 0.066 to 0.478, but count-based AUROC stays near chance (0.495-0.526). Newer CodeQL releases attain higher F1 alongside nearly parallel rises in recall and false-positive rate, not stronger separation of vulnerable from fixed cases. In project-matched year pairs, CodeQL R2024 has negative mean later-minus-earlier F1 at every source-year gap, whereas Infer v1.1 and v1.3 have positive means throughout. Among selected drops, only 6 of 39 CodeQL and 2 of 620 Infer findings overlap a changed repair line. For Semgrep, 78.96% of cases show parser or timeout diagnostics even though every run reports success. These results suggest that apparent changes in temporal SAST effectiveness can arise from broader alerting, changing analysis coverage, and incidental findings, not solely from losses in vulnerability detection. Evaluations of temporal sustainability should fix detector conditions, control for projects, inspect repair-level evidence, and report failed or degraded analyses.
articles.title_ja: 固定された検出器、動くコード：1年間にわたるC/C++の進化において静的セキュリティアナライザーはどの程度耐えうるか？
articles.summary_ja: 静的アプリケーションセキュリティテスト（SAST）ツールが将来のコードや未知の脆弱性に対してどれほど効果を維持できるかを検証するため、2016年から2025年までの1,116のオープンソースプロジェクトから抽出された20,000件の脆弱・修正済みC/C++ケースを用いて評価が行われた。CodeQL、Infer、Semgrepを用い、時間経過による影響とコード構成の変化を区別して分析した結果、見かけ上の有効性の変化は広範な警告や解析カバレッジの変化、偶発的な発見に起因する場合があることが示された。評価においては、検出器条件の固定、プロジェクトの制御、修復レベルのエッジケースの検証が必要とされる。

articles.title: CloakFEM: Agentic FEM Code Generation for Red-Teaming Computational Resource Exhaustion
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.04356v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Finite element method (FEM) solvers are foundational to scientific and engineering simulation, yet their susceptibility to \emph{efficiency attacks} remains largely unexplored. An adversary can craft syntactically valid and runnable FEM programs that complete successfully while forcing excessive computational work, enabling computational denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. Finding such inputs is challenging because FEM programs occupy a vast, structured space constrained by numerical, geometric, and constitutive requirements. We introduce CloakFEM, a domain-guided LLM-agent framework for automatically generating runnable adversarial FEM programs that amplify solver computation. CloakFEM combines LLM-guided search with an FEM-specific intermediate representation and a deterministic validity gate that enforces runnable constraints. Across three FEM stacks, 17 problem classes, and 1,068 seeds, CloakFEM discovers adversarial inputs that substantially amplify solver work while remaining valid and solvable. In the most extreme case, solver iterations increase from 43 to 247,367, a \(5{,}752.72\times\) amplification. CloakFEM outperforms five generic black-box baselines and retains an advantage over evolutionary search under a controlled bounded action space. Cross-solver analysis further reveals both problem-intrinsic and solver-specific sources of vulnerability. Our results uncover an underexplored efficiency-attack surface in FEM solvers and show that runnable FEM programs can serve as adversarial inputs.

articles.title: Grammar-Constrained Decoding Can Jailbreak LLMs into Generating Malicious Code
articles.summary:
arXiv:2606.11817v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for code generation, raising concerns that they may be misused to produce malicious code. Meanwhile, Grammar-Constrained Decoding (GCD) has been widely adopted to improve the reliability of LLM-generated code by enforcing syntactic validity. In this paper, we reveal a counterintuitive risk: this reliability-oriented technique can itself become an attack surface. We uncover a new jailbreak attack, termed CodeSpear, that exploits GCD to induce LLMs into generating malicious code. Our experiments show that simply applying a benign code grammar constraint can effectively jailbreak LLMs.
  To address this vulnerability, we propose CodeShield, a safety alignment approach that robustly preserves safe behavior even under attacker-controlled grammar constraints. CodeShield aligns the model in the code modality by teaching it to generate honeypot code under GCD. Such code is semantically harmless, so it does not implement the malicious request, and structurally diverse, so it is difficult to suppress through grammar tightening. At the same time, CodeShield still preserves natural-language refusals when natural language is available. Experiments on 10 popular LLMs across 4 benchmarks show that CodeSpear outperforms representative jailbreak baselines and increases the attack success rate by more than 30 percentage points on average. CodeShield also restores safety under CodeSpear while preserving benign utility. Our findings reveal a fundamental risk of GCD and call for greater attention to its potential security implications.

articles.title: A Compact Formula-Aware Spreadsheet Abstraction for Large Language Models
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.03705v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to assist spreadsheet users with tasks such as spreadsheet model construction, formula generation, and data analysis, yet their interaction with real-world spreadsheets remains limited by the mismatch between the structure of spreadsheets and the sequential textual representations typically provided to LLMs. We propose a compact formula-aware spreadsheet abstraction that represents large homogeneous ranges through their positions, types, R1C1 formula patterns, and selected boundary values. An efficient algorithm detects and structures these ranges before a textual serialization is supplied to an LLM. The abstraction is provided to the LLM before detailed spreadsheet content is submitted, improving the accuracy and efficiency of spreadsheet processing while reducing token consumption. We evaluate the method on 50 spreadsheet-query cases. The evaluation shows that the abstraction alone was sufficient to answer some queries. When additional spreadsheet content is required, the abstraction reduces the amount of data that must be submitted to the LLM, thereby reducing token consumption. The abstraction layer also improves the reliability and accuracy of spreadsheet processing. We conclude by discussing further techniques for combining spreadsheet static analysis with artificial intelligence to improve the reliability, accuracy, and efficiency of AI assisted spreadsheet tasks.

articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.04456v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model-based agents increasingly rely on external skills to reuse task-specific knowledge without retraining the model. As skills become common for extending agent capabilities, understanding creation and evolution is critical for reliable agent systems. However, existing studies mainly examine agent skills from a static perspective, leaving their evolution in real-world repositories largely unexplored. This limits our understanding of the patterns and motivations behind skill changes. To fill this gap, we present a large-scale empirical study of agent skills, capturing 84,200 skills and 750,898 commits from GitHub. We manually construct taxonomies of skill components, change patterns, and evolution motivations, and build an automated annotation pipeline to label changes at scale. Based on the taxonomy, we conduct quantitative analyses of skill composition and post-creation evolution frequency, together with qualitative assessments of modified components, change patterns, and motivations. Our findings reveal five implications: (i) reliability receives less attention in skill composition and change, motivating execution-contract skill design that incorporates verification and recovery mechanisms; (ii) evolution changes concentrate in project-coupled skills, calling for automated just-in-time skill updating mechanisms; (iii) change patterns are dominated by incremental enrichment and refinement, motivating pattern-guided skill enhancers that diagnose and improve incomplete skill components; (iv) redundancy is a practical maintenance issue, highlighting the need for context-efficient skill representation; (v) security-motivated changes show limited risk reduction, suggesting skill regression testing methods that objectively verify skill functionality and security. Beyond these insights, our dataset provides a basis for future studies on automated skill techniques.

articles.title: PentestEval: Benchmarking LLM-based Penetration Testing with Modular and Stage-Level Design
articles.summary:
arXiv:2512.14233v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Penetration testing is essential for assessing and strengthening system security against real-world threats, yet traditional workflows remain highly manual, expertise-intensive, and difficult to scale. Although recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) offer promising opportunities for automation, existing applications rely on simplistic prompting without task decomposition or domain adaptation, resulting in unreliable black-box behavior and limited insight into model capabilities across penetration testing stages. To address this gap, we introduce PentestEval, the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLMs across six decomposed penetration testing stages: Information Collection, Weakness Gathering and Filtering, Attack Decision-Making, Exploit Generation and Revision. PentestEval integrates expert-annotated ground truth with a fully automated evaluation pipeline across 346 tasks covering all stages in 12 realistic vulnerable scenarios. Our stage-level evaluation of 9 widely used LLMs reveals generally weak performance and distinct limitations across the stages of penetration-testing workflow. End-to-end pipelines reach only 31% success rate, and existing LLM-powered systems such as PentestGPT, PentestAgent, and VulnBot exhibit similar limitations, with the evaluated autonomous agents showing particularly low success rates under our benchmark settings. These findings highlight that reliable autonomous penetration testing requires stronger structured reasoning and fine-grained stage-level diagnosis. PentestEval provides the foundational benchmark needed for future research on fine-grained, stage-level evaluation, paving the way toward more reliable LLM-based automation.

articles.title: How Safe Are AI-Generated Patches? A Large-scale Study on Security Risks in LLM and Agentic Automated Program Repair on SWE-bench
articles.summary:
arXiv:2507.02976v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) and agentic frameworks are increasingly used for development tasks such as automated program repair (APR). Prior work has identified security risks in LLM-generated code, but most studies focus on synthetic, simplified, or isolated tasks. We present a large-scale security analysis of LLM-generated patches using 20,000+ GitHub issues from SWE-bench. We evaluate developer-written patches, two standalone LLMs (Llama 3.3 Instruct-70B and GPT-5.4 nano), and four agentic frameworks (OpenHands, AutoCodeRover, HoneyComb, and SWE-agent). We also analyze code, issue, and project-level factors associated with insecure patches. Under our evaluated SWE-bench setup, Llama 3.3 introduced 135 manually confirmed vulnerabilities across the train and test sets, compared with 12 in developer-written patches for the same issues. On the SWE-bench test set, GPT-5.4 nano introduced 3 vulnerabilities compared with 2 in developer patches. All four evaluated agentic frameworks also introduced vulnerabilities. OpenHands had the highest retained count, with 44 vulnerabilities across 11 issue instances. Vulnerabilities are associated with broader code modifications and with issues missing specific information. These results suggest that APR systems require proactive risk assessment methods that consider both generated code and issue context.

articles.title: Price is Only the Symptom: Understanding and Analyzing Economic-State Manipulation Vulnerabilities in DeFi
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.00587v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Economic-state manipulation has emerged as a significant security threat to decentralized finance (DeFi), causing substantial financial losses. Existing studies predominantly characterize these attacks as price manipulation, focusing on observable price distortions while overlooking underlying violations of economic-state integrity. We conduct a comprehensive empirical study of Economic-State Manipulation (ESM) vulnerabilities in DeFi. We first curate a diverse dataset comprising 276 real-world attacks and 91 Code4rena audit findings. Based on these cases, we develop a cause-oriented taxonomy comprising four primary categories and eleven subcategories. Our analysis reveals that ESM vulnerabilities extend beyond conventional price manipulation, frequently involving violations of protocol-internal accounting, AMM state consistency, and execution-time constraints. We further investigate the evaluation datasets of six existing studies and find that, although they cover 6-10 vulnerability subcategories, their distributions remain dominated by limited manipulation mechanisms. Furthermore, we systematically evaluate seven representative detection approaches on our dataset. Our results reveal limited coverage, with the best-performing approach identifying only 50.4% of real-world attacks. Through an analysis of false negatives and false positives, we identify fundamental limitations arising from reliance on predefined attack patterns, insufficient reasoning about economic-state semantics, and incomplete exploitability validation. These findings provide empirical insights for developing more generalizable ESM vulnerability detection techniques.

articles.title: StateGate: A Behavioral-Fidelity Prompt Optimization Method for Long-Chain LLM Agents
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.01585v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Currently, long-chain LLM agents commonly suffer from behavioral degradation in complex tasks, where prompts are written in full but steps are not executed in full. To address this issue, existing approaches face three major challenges. First, constraints are strongly bound to their textual carriers; once natural-language constraint sentences are removed, their binding force vanishes. Second, the execution process lacks independent verification, as the evidence for judgment is often supplied by the executing party itself, leading to the failure of self-referential validation. Third, existing remediation schemes are difficult to generalize, and hard-coded mechanisms cannot be transferred across tasks. In this paper, we propose StateGate, a novel prompt-optimization scheme that transforms semantic constraints into symbolic gates enforced by an external deterministic runtime. By decoupling the content of a constraint from its carrier of efficacy, StateGate achieves behavioral fidelity in long-chain tasks without losing the binding force of the prompt. Specifically, we first propose four independent compression strategies (deduplication, generalization, externalization, and text-to-gating) together with their corresponding decision chains, enabling principled prompt symbolization. Second, we design a three-component architecture consisting of a state file, a validator, and an orchestrator, which thoroughly separates judgment authority from execution authority. Third, we formally prove that the compliance of symbolic constraints is independent of context size. Finally, we validate the framework on a vulnerability-discovery task in the security domain; the results show that StateGate achieves 100% execution closure and accurate vulnerability detection.

articles.summary_ja: 長鎖LLMエージェントが複雑なタスクでステップを完全に実行しない行動劣化問題に対し、意味的制約を外部の決定論的ランタイムによって強制されるシンボリックゲートに変換するプロンプト最適化手法「StateGate」を提案している。状態ファイル、バリデーター、オーケストレーターからなる3コンポーネントアーキテクチャにより、判断権限と実行権限を完全に分離する。セキュリティ分野の脆弱性発見タスクでの検証では、100%の実行完了率と正確な脆弱性検知を達成したことを示している。

articles.title: Refusing the Impossible: A Taxonomy and Benchmark for Code Hallucination in Large Language Models
articles.summary:
arXiv:2609.03267v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: This paper investigates whether large language models (LLMs) for code generation can recognize a programming request that cannot be satisfied. Coding assistants are widely deployed, yet they are evaluated almost exclusively on solvable tasks where a test suite can score the output. A request may instead name a package that does not exist or ask for an algorithm that is mathematically impossible, and the appropriate response is to refuse. Models nevertheless respond with plausible code, and such fabrications are also a security concern because attackers can register the package names that models invent. We define code hallucination as ungrounded code generation, distinguish it from ordinary programming errors, and introduce a taxonomy of these failures together with a benchmark of 270 adversarial requests and 91 matched solvable controls across six languages and 24 subcategories. We evaluate 17 open-weight models with 6.7B to 671B parameters, collecting 6,137 responses. Models hallucinate on 54% of the adversarial requests and correctly refuse 31%. Larger models do better on algorithmic impossibilities and conflicting requirements, where hallucination falls from 84% for models at or below 7B parameters to 32% for those at or above 80B. For plausible but nonexistent dependencies and features, the rates are 88% and 61%, and even the largest model hallucinates on all 22 requests for nonexistent JavaScript and Rust packages. Two-thirds of hallucinations are confident fabrications without caveats, and some reasoning models fail to return an answer on solvable tasks. Scale teaches models to recognize what is impossible but not what does not exist, so grounding code generation in the real software ecosystem, for example by checking package names against registries, remains necessary regardless of model size.

articles.title: From Stories to Bugs: Story-Based Semantic Fuzzing of Interactive Systems
articles.summary:
arXiv:2611.01173v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Complex interactive systems hide business-logic failures along two complementary axes: deep state-dependent behaviors that require long valid prefixes and concurrency-sensitive failures that depend on the ordering of otherwise legal operations. We present story-based semantic fuzzing, a methodology that treats semantically constrained compositions of behavioral stories as primary search objects. Implemented through Behavioral Programming, semantic binding and state constraints preserve legal prefixes, while event eligibility, schedule selection, and replay expose failure-relevant interleavings. We evaluate the methodology on Magento and four stateful REST APIs. On Magento, overlap-aware ranking increased reproduction of a sporadic Shipping Fee race from 3.6% to 41.2%; a controlled ordering intervention reduced a second failure signature from 100/100 initial executions to 0/200 constrained executions. For the REST study, a versioned end-to-end pipeline took each frozen public OpenAPI contract as its sole benchmark-specific model-generation input and automatically generated the Basic and Complex stories, dependency structure, and interface bindings. Under a shared black-box task and sequence-local evaluation contract, Basic and Complex confirmed 0/11 and 11/11 semantic fault classes, while RESTler and EvoMaster confirmed 2/11 and 0/11. A paired binding ablation produced 250/250 valid dependent operations with binding and 0/250 without it, while supplementary prefix controls localized the difference to preservation of legal relational state. Together, the studies show that searching admissible semantic compositions provides a unified and effective representation for reaching deep states and exposing concurrency-sensitive business-logic failures.

Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly used to automate vulnerability detection, but reliable detection is challenging because agents must distinguish subtle, security-relevant fixes from benign code variation. Harnesses are typically fixed, and largely hand-written, limiting adaptat
articles.title_ja: LLMエージェントによる脆弱性検知の課題とHarness自動発見手法「MetaVul」の提案

articles.insight: AI関連のインシデント（Anthropic、Cloudflare AIデータ漏洩、AI駆動マルウェア）が複数報告されていることは、AIエコシステム全体のセキュリティリスクが高まっていることを示唆します。CDCは、AIシステムのライフサイクル全体におけるリスク評価（Security for AI）と、AIを活用した脅威検知・対応（AI for Security）の両面で戦略を加速させる必要があります。特に、UEFIのような基盤コンポーネントの脆弱性は広範な影響を持つため、Exposure管理の継続的な強化が求められます。
articles.importance_reason: 複数のセキュリティ事象がAI関連のトレンドを示唆しており、CDCにおける広範なリスク認識と対応戦略の検討に資するため中程度の重要性です。

articles.title: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts
articles.summary:
How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts

Parameter Labs describe an exploit they found against ChatGPT's implementation of the artifacts pattern (OpenAI used to call this "Canvas" but it looks like the latest revision is called HTML previews), where interactive custom HTML apps are displayed in a sa
articles.title_ja: ChatGPTアカウント乗っ取りの手口を解説
articles.summary_ja: Parameter Labsが、ChatGPTのHTMLプレビュー機能（以前はCanvasと呼ばれたartifactsパターン）の実装における脆弱性を悪用し、ChatGPTアカウントを乗っ取る方法を公開しました。これは、インタラクティブなカスタムHTMLアプリの表示メカニズムに関連するものです。
articles.insight: LLMベースのアプリケーション（ChatGPT）における脆弱性は、Security for AIの具体的な課題を示しています。特に、ユーザーインタフェースや機能拡張（例: HTMLプレビュー、カスタムツール実行）が、プロンプトインジェクションやコード実行の新たな経路となり得ます。CDCは、LLMアプリケーションのログ（プロンプト履歴、API呼び出し、外部ツール実行、セッション情報）を監視し、異常な挙動や権限濫用を検知するルールを開発する必要があります。AIエージェントリスク6階層モデルの「モデル・推論層」と「ツール・実行層」に直接関連します。
articles.importance_reason: LLMアプリケーション固有の脆弱性を悪用した具体的なアカウント乗っ取り事例であり、Security for AIの設計・運用に直接的な示唆を与えるため重要です。
tag_subs: プロンプトインジェクション

articles.title: Devs Hit by Trojanized Claude Code Extension for Cursor
articles.summary: Two serious security issues hit Cursor on the same day, highlighting the risks for AI-powered integrated development environments (IDEs).
articles.title_ja: AI搭載IDE「Cursor」でトロイの木馬化されたClaudeコード拡張機能による被害
articles.summary_ja: AI搭載統合開発環境（IDE）であるCursorにおいて、トロイの木馬化されたClaudeコード拡張機能による深刻なセキュリティ問題が報告されました。これは、AIを活用したIDEの利用における新たなリスクを浮き彫りにしています。
articles.insight: 記事2と連携し、AI搭載IDEのような開発者向けツールのセキュリティが脆弱であると、サプライチェーン攻撃の温床となるリスクを示唆します。CDCは、開発者環境の監視を強化し、AI開発パイプラインにおけるセキュリティ対策（Secure by Design、SSLC）を支援する必要があります。特に、CI/CDツールやレポジトリのログ、開発者エンドポイントでの不審なプロセス実行やネットワーク通信を監視対象に追加し、AIエージェントリスク6階層モデルの「ツール・実行層」および「組織・ガバナンス層」への対策を検討するべきです。
articles.importance_reason: AI開発環境における具体的なサプライチェーン攻撃の事例であり、Security for AIの設計とSOC/CDCの監視対象拡大に直接的な影響を与えるため重要です。
tag_subs: サプライチェーン攻撃

articles.title: Behind the Scenes of How Operation Blackout Went Down
articles.summary: A recent law enforcement operation to dismantle harmful scam centers was a big success. A threat intelligence expert walks us through what happened and why he wants more of the same.
articles.title_ja: 「Operation Blackout」の舞台裏：詐欺センター解体の成功事例
articles.summary_ja: 最近の法執行機関による詐欺センター解体作戦「Operation Blackout」は大きな成功を収めました。脅威インテリジェンスの専門家がその経緯と、なぜこのような作戦が今後も重要であるかを説明しています。
articles.insight: 法執行機関と脅威インテリジェンスの連携によるサイバー犯罪組織の撲滅は、攻撃者側の活動抑制に貢献します。CDCの運用においては、単なる技術的な監視だけでなく、このような脅威インテリジェンスを積極的に取り入れ、攻撃者プロファイルの理解を深めることが、より効果的な検知ルールや対応策の策定に繋がります。特に、顧客組織が標的となる可能性のある脅威グループの動向をCISO報告に含めることは、経営層のリスク認識を高める上で有効です。
articles.importance_reason: 直接的なSOC/CDCの技術・運用変更に関するものではないが、脅威インテリジェンス活用の重要性を再認識させる事例であるため低程度の重要性です。
related_keywords: 脅威インテリジェンス

articles.title: Passkeys Are Better Than Passwords. But They Are Not Enough.
articles.summary:
As organizations eliminate passwords, attackers will adapt. Instead of attacking the authenticator directly, they will look for opportunities around it.

The post Passkeys Are Better Than Passwords. But They Are Not Enough. appeared first on SecurityWeek.
articles.title_ja: パスキーは優れているが、それだけでは不十分
articles.summary_ja: パスキーはパスワードよりも優れた認証方式ですが、組織がパスワードを廃止しても攻撃者は適応し、認証器自体を狙うのではなく、その周辺の脆弱性を探すようになります。
articles.insight: 認証技術の進化（パスキーの普及）は、Identity/ITDRの防御を強化する一方で、攻撃者が新たな経路（例えば、セッション管理、認証後の権限、関連するデータ流通）を狙うことを示唆しています。CDCは、認証方式が高度化しても、認証プロセス全体の堅牢性を確認し、セッションハイジャック、認証後の横展開、不正なAPIアクセスなど、認証周辺のリスクに対する監視と検知ルールを強化する必要があります。これはMDR/MSSPが提供すべきIdentity/ITDRサービスの進化にも繋がります。
articles.importance_reason: 認証トレンドの変化はIdentity/ITDRの設計やSOCの監視対象に影響を与え、中長期的な防御アーキテクチャに示唆を与えるため中程度の重要性です。
